title.zh: 卷二百四十五 列傳第四 宗室二
title.raw: 卷二百四十五 列傳第四 宗室二 Volume 245 Biographies 4: Imperial Clan 2

sentences.zh: 宗室二

translations.literal: Imperial Clan 2
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Clan, Part Two

sentences.zh: 漢王元佐 昭成太子元僖 商王元份 越王元傑 鎮王元偓 楚王元偁 周王元儼 悼獻太子 濮王允讓

translations.literal: Prince of Han Yuanzuo; Heir Apparent Zhaocheng Yuanxi; Prince of Shang Yuanfen; Prince of Yue Yuanjie; Prince of Zhen Yuanwei; Prince of Chu Yuancheng; Prince of Zhou Yuanyan; Heir Apparent Daoxian; Prince of Pu Yunrang
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Han Yuanzuo; Heir Apparent Zhaocheng Yuanxi; Prince of Shang Yuanfen; Prince of Yue Yuanjie; Prince of Zhen Yuanwei; Prince of Chu Yuancheng; Prince of Zhou Yuanyan; Heir Apparent Daoxian; Prince of Pu Yunrang

sentences.zh: 太宗九子：長楚王元佐，次昭成太子元僖，次真宗，次商恭靖王元份，次越文惠王元傑，次鎮恭懿王元偓，次楚恭惠王元偁，次周恭肅王元儼，次崇王元億。

translations.literal: Taizong had nine sons: the eldest was Prince of Chu Yuanzuo; next Heir Apparent Zhaocheng Yuanxi; next Zhenzong; next Prince of Shang, Respectful and Tranquil, Yuanfen; next Prince of Yue, Cultured and Kind, Yuanjie; next Prince of Zhen, Respectful and Virtuous, Yuanwei; next Prince of Chu, Respectful and Gracious, Yuancheng; next Prince of Zhou, Respectful and Solemn, Yuanyan; next Prince of Chong Yuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had nine sons: the eldest was Prince of Chu Yuanzuo; next came Heir Apparent Zhaocheng Yuanxi; then Zhenzong; then Prince of Shang Yuanfen, posthumously titled Respectful and Tranquil; then Prince of Yue Yuanjie, Cultured and Kind; then Prince of Zhen Yuanwei, Respectful and Virtuous; then Prince of Chu Yuancheng, Respectful and Gracious; then Prince of Zhou Yuanyan, Respectful and Solemn; and lastly Prince of Chong Yuanyi.

sentences.zh: 漢王元佐

translations.literal: Prince of Han Yuanzuo
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Han Yuanzuo

sentences.zh: 漢恭憲王元佐字惟吉，初名德崇，母元德皇后。

translations.literal: Prince of Han, Respectful and Magnanimous, Yuanzuo, courtesy name Weiji, original name Dechong; his mother was Empress Yuande.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzuo, Prince of Han, posthumously titled Respectful and Magnanimous, whose courtesy name was Weiji and whose original name was Dechong, was born to Empress Yuande.

sentences.zh: 少聰警，貌類太宗，帝鍾愛之。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and alert; his appearance resembled Taizong's, and the emperor cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick-witted and sharp, and because he resembled Emperor Taizong in looks, the emperor doted on him.

sentences.zh: 年十三，從獵近郊，兔走乘輿前，太宗使元佐射，一發而中，契丹使在側，驚異之。

translations.literal: At age thirteen, on a hunt near the capital, a hare ran before the imperial carriage; Taizong had Yuanzuo shoot, and with one shot he hit it; Khitan envoys at the side were startled and amazed.
translations.idiomatic: When he was thirteen, on a hunt in the suburbs, a hare dashed in front of the imperial carriage. Taizong ordered Yuanzuo to shoot, and he brought it down at the first shot. Khitan envoys standing nearby were astonished.

sentences.zh: 從征太原、幽薊。

translations.literal: He followed the campaigns against Taiyuan and You-Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the expeditions against Taiyuan and the You-Ji region.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，出居內東門別第，拜檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事，封衞王，赴上于中書。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo era he moved out to a separate residence at the Inner Eastern Gate, was appointed Grand Tutor by inspection and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, and attended court at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo period he took up residence in a separate mansion at the Inner Eastern Gate, was appointed honorary Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, and presented himself at the Secretariat for his investiture.

sentences.zh: 後徙居東宮，改賜今名，加檢校太尉，進封楚王。

translations.literal: Later he moved to the Eastern Palace; he was granted his present name, promoted to honorary Grand Marshal, and advanced to Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later moved to the Eastern Palace, given his present name, promoted to honorary Grand Marshal, and raised to Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 初，秦王廷美遷涪陵，元佐獨申救之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Prince of Qin Tingmei was banished to Fuling, Yuanzuo alone pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Prince of Qin Tingmei was exiled to Fuling, Yuanzuo alone interceded for him.

sentences.zh: 廷美死，元佐遂發狂，至以小過操挺刃傷侍人。

translations.literal: When Tingmei died, Yuanzuo thereupon went mad, even taking up a staff or blade over trifles to wound attendants.
translations.idiomatic: After Tingmei's death Yuanzuo lost his mind, going so far as to seize a club or blade over minor provocations and injure his attendants.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，疾少間，帝喜，為赦天下。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi his illness eased somewhat; the emperor rejoiced and proclaimed an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi his illness briefly improved. The emperor was delighted and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 重陽日內宴，元佐疾新愈不與，諸王宴歸，暮過元佐第。

translations.literal: On the Double Ninth there was an inner palace banquet; Yuanzuo, having only just recovered, was not invited; when the princes returned from the feast at dusk they passed by Yuanzuo's residence.
translations.idiomatic: On the Double Ninth Festival the court held an inner banquet. Yuanzuo, still convalescent, was not invited. When the other princes came back from the feast at dusk, they passed Yuanzuo's mansion.

sentences.zh: 曰

translations.literal: said
translations.idiomatic: He said

sentences.zh: 〈「曰」：按《宋會要》帝系二之二、《長編》卷二六記本條事都作「元佐謂曰」，疑此上有脫文。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "said": According to Song Huiyao, Imperial Lineage 2.2, and Comprehensive Chronicle, juan 26, this entry reads "Yuanzuo addressed them, saying"; it is suspected that text is missing above.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note on "said": The Song Huiyao (Imperial Lineage 2.2) and the Comprehensive Chronicle, juan 26, both read "Yuanzuo addressed them, saying" for this passage; text is probably missing above this point.〉

sentences.zh: ：「若等侍上宴，我獨不與，是棄我也。」

translations.literal: : "You all waited on the emperor at the banquet while I alone was not included—this is to cast me aside."
translations.idiomatic: : "You all attended the emperor's banquet while I alone was left out. You have abandoned me."

sentences.zh: 遂發忿，被酒，夜縱火焚宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he flew into rage, was drunk with wine, and in the night set fire and burned the palace.
translations.idiomatic: With that he gave way to fury. Drunk, he set the palace ablaze that night.

sentences.zh: 詔遣御史捕元佐，詣中書劾問，廢為庶人，均州安置。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched censors to seize Yuanzuo, bring him to the Secretariat for impeachment and interrogation, depose him as a commoner, and settle him in Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent censors to arrest Yuanzuo and bring him before the Secretariat for investigation. He was deposed to commoner status and placed under residence order in Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 宰相宋琪率百官三上表，請留元佐京師。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Song Qi led the hundred officials in submitting three memorials asking that Yuanzuo be kept in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Song Qi led the officials in three memorials asking that Yuanzuo be kept in the capital.

sentences.zh: 行至黃山，召還，廢居南宮，使者守護。

translations.literal: When he reached Huangshan he was summoned back, deposed and lodged in the Southern Palace, with envoys guarding him.
translations.idiomatic: When he had reached Huangshan he was recalled, confined in the Southern Palace as a deposed prince, and placed under guard.

sentences.zh: 諮議趙齊王遹、翊善戴元頓首請罪，帝赦之曰：「是子朕教之猶不悛，汝等安能輔導耶？」

translations.literal: Advisers Zhao Qi, Wang Suo, and Instructor Dai Yuan kowtowed and begged forgiveness; the emperor pardoned them, saying: "This son I myself taught, yet he will not reform—how could you guide him?"
translations.idiomatic: Advisers Zhao Qi and Wang Suo and instructor Dai Yuan kowtowed to beg forgiveness. The emperor pardoned them, saying, "I myself taught this son, yet he would not mend his ways—how could you have guided him?"

sentences.zh: 仁宗

translations.literal: Renzong
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong

sentences.zh: 〈「仁宗」：原作「神宗」，據《宋會要》帝系四之七、《長編》卷一五一、《通考》卷二七七封建考改。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "Renzong": the original read "Shenzong"; emended according to Song Huiyao, Imperial Lineage 4.7, Comprehensive Chronicle juan 151, and Tongkao juan 277, Enfeoffment.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note on "Renzong": the original text read "Shenzong"; it is emended to "Renzong" on the authority of the Song Huiyao (Imperial Lineage 4.7), the Comprehensive Chronicle, juan 151, and the Tongkao, juan 277 (Enfeoffment).〉

sentences.zh: 封王後，以允言子宗說恭憲王長孫，嗣封祁國公。

translations.literal: After enfeoffment as king, Yunyuan's son Zongshuo, eldest grandson of the Respectful and Magnanimous Prince, succeeded to the enfeoffment as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: After the title of king was conferred, Zongshuo, son of Yunyuan and eldest grandson of the Respectful and Magnanimous Prince, succeeded to the enfeoffment as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，坐帷薄不修除名，又坐坑殺女僕，鎖閉宮室外宅。

translations.literal: In Huangyou, for improper conduct within the women's quarters he was struck from the rolls; again, for burying alive a maidservant, he was locked up in an outer residence of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou he was struck from the rolls for disorder in the inner quarters, and later, for burying a maidservant alive, he was confined to an outer palace residence.

sentences.zh: 其子仲旻，官右武衞大將軍、道州刺史，後因朝，叩頭殿下泣訴云：「父老且病，願納身官以贖。」

translations.literal: His son Zhongmin, holding office as General of the Right Martial Guards and Prefect of Daozhou, later on attending court kowtowed below the hall and wept, pleading: "My father is old and ill; I wish to surrender my own offices in ransom."
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongmin, who held the posts of General of the Right Martial Guards and Prefect of Daozhou, later came to court, kowtowed below the steps, and wept as he pleaded: "My father is old and ill. I beg to give up my own offices to redeem him."

sentences.zh: 神宗亦愍之，而未俞其請。

translations.literal: Shenzong also pitied him, but did not approve the request.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong pitied him as well, but did not grant the request.

sentences.zh: 出就馬，氣塞不能言，及家而卒。

translations.literal: Going out to mount his horse, his breath choked and he could not speak; by the time he reached home he had died.
translations.idiomatic: As he went out to mount his horse, grief choked him so that he could not speak, and he died before reaching home.

sentences.zh: 贈同州觀察使、馮翊侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Commissioner of Tongzhou and Marquis of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Commissioner of Tongzhou and Marquis of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 宗說幽死。

translations.literal: Zongshuo died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshuo died in secret confinement.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，以允升子宗惠襲封魏國公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, Yunsheng's son Zonghui succeeded to the enfeoffment as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining, Zonghui, son of Yunsheng, succeeded to the enfeoffment as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 中書言宗惠不應封，以恭憲庶長孫允言子宗立嗣。

translations.literal: The Secretariat said Zonghui should not be enfeoffed; the eldest grandson by a secondary wife of the Respectful and Magnanimous Prince, Yunyuan's son Zongli, was made heir.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat held that Zonghui was not eligible for the title, and installed Zongli, son of Yunyuan and eldest grandson of the Respectful and Magnanimous Prince by a secondary wife, as successor.

sentences.zh: 宗立從張揆學春秋。

translations.literal: Zongli studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Zhang Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Zongli studied the Spring and Autumn Annals under Zhang Kui.

sentences.zh: 太清樓侍宴，預坐悉賦祼玉詩，宗立詩先成，仁宗稱善。

translations.literal: At a banquet in the Taiqing Pavilion, all who were seated beforehand composed poems on the theme of naked jade; Zongli's poem was finished first, and Renzong praised it.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in the Taiqing Pavilion, every guest present was asked to compose a poem on the theme of "Naked Jade." Zongli finished first, and Emperor Renzong commended it.

sentences.zh: 屢賜飛白書，旌其文雅。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly granted flying-white calligraphy to honor his literary refinement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly bestowed flying-white calligraphy to honor his literary accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 至是襲封，終武寧軍節度觀察留後，贈昭信軍節度使、同中書門下平章事、南康郡王。

translations.literal: At this time he succeeded to the enfeoffment; he ended as Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Wuning, posthumously made Military Commissioner of Zhaoxin, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Prince of Nankang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He then took up the succession, served finally as Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Wuning, and was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Zhaoxin, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 子仲來嗣，終金州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Zhonglai succeeded; he ended as Prefect of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhonglai succeeded him and ended his career as Prefect of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 子不儻嗣子不儻嗣，不儻是仲來之孫，但所記仲來、不儻官爵都與本傳不同，不儻亦無後。

translations.literal: Son Butang succeeded; son Butang succeeded—Butang was Zhonglai's grandson, but the recorded offices and titles of Zhonglai and Butang all differ from this biography, and Butang also had no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: The text reads "son Butang succeeded; son Butang succeeded." Butang was Zhonglai's grandson, but the offices and titles recorded for Zhonglai and Butang all differ from this biography, and Butang likewise left no heirs.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，改封魏王為漢王。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne, the enfeoffment of Prince of Wei was changed to Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong acceded, the title Prince of Wei was changed to Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 不儻卒，子彥清乞襲父爵，奉漢王祀，詔從之。

translations.literal: When Butang died, his son Yanqing begged to succeed to his father's rank and perform sacrifices to the Prince of Han; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When Butang died, his son Yanqing petitioned to inherit his father's title and maintain the sacrifices to the Prince of Han. The court granted the request.

sentences.zh: 允升字吉先，初免乳，養明德太后宮，太后親撫視之。

translations.literal: Yunsheng, courtesy name Jixian; when first weaned from the breast he was reared in Empress Dowager Mingde's palace, and the empress dowager personally cared for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunsheng, whose courtesy name was Jixian, was weaned early and raised in Empress Dowager Mingde's palace, where the empress dowager personally looked after him.

sentences.zh: 元佐有疾，允升始出第。

translations.literal: When Yuanzuo fell ill, Yunsheng first left the palace residence.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Yuanzuo fell ill did Yunsheng leave the palace residence.

sentences.zh: 真宗賜名元中，授右監門衞將軍，更賜今名。

translations.literal: Zhenzong granted the name Yuanzhong and appointed him General of the Right Gate Guards, then granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong gave him the name Yuanzhong and appointed him General of the Right Gate Guards, then bestowed his present name.

sentences.zh: 累遷澶州觀察使，封延安郡公，進武寧軍節度觀察留後，歷安德、建雄、安國軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Commissioner of Chanzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan'an Commandery, advanced to Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Wuning, and served as Military Commissioner of Ande, Jianxiong, and Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Commissioner of Chanzhou, was enfeoffed Duke of Yan'an, advanced to Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Wuning, and held successive commands as Military Commissioner of Ande, Jianxiong, and Anguo.

sentences.zh: 景祐二年卒，贈太尉、平陽郡王，謚懿恭。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Jingyou; posthumously made Grand Marshal and Prince of Pingyang Commandery, posthumous title Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Jingyou and was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Prince of Pingyang, with the posthumous title Respectful and Reverent.

sentences.zh: 子十三人，宗禮、宗旦、宗悌、宗惠知名。

translations.literal: He had thirteen sons; Zongli, Zongdan, Zongti, and Zonghui were well known.
translations.idiomatic: He had thirteen sons, of whom Zongli, Zongdan, Zongti, and Zonghui were the most notable.

sentences.zh: 宗禮嘗侍宴太清樓，仁宗賦詩，命屬和，侍射苑中，復獻詩。

translations.literal: Zongli once attended a banquet in the Taiqing Pavilion; Renzong composed a poem and ordered him to harmonize; attending an archery gathering in the park, he again presented a poem.
translations.idiomatic: Zongli once attended a banquet in the Taiqing Pavilion. Emperor Renzong composed a poem and ordered him to supply a matching verse; at an archery gathering in the imperial park he presented another poem.

sentences.zh: 終虔州觀察使、成國公，贈宗禮嘗侍宴太清樓，仁宗賦詩，命屬和，侍射苑中，復獻詩。

translations.literal: He ended as Commissioner of Qianzhou and Duke of Cheng; posthumously—Zongli once attended a banquet in the Taiqing Pavilion, Renzong composed a poem, ordered him to harmonize, attended an archery gathering in the park, and again presented a poem.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Commissioner of Qianzhou and Duke of Cheng; the posthumous entry repeats: Zongli once attended a banquet in the Taiqing Pavilion, Emperor Renzong composed a poem and ordered him to harmonize, and at an archery gathering in the park he again presented a poem.

sentences.zh: 終虔州觀察使、成國公，贈安遠軍節度使、同中書門下平章事、韓國公。

translations.literal: He ended as Commissioner of Qianzhou and Duke of Cheng; posthumously made Military Commissioner of Anyuan, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Duke of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Commissioner of Qianzhou and Duke of Cheng, and was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Anyuan, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 子仲翹、仲髦。

translations.literal: Sons Zhongqiao and Zhongmao.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhongqiao and Zhongmao.

sentences.zh: 宗旦字子文，七歲如成人，選為仁宗伴讀。

translations.literal: Zongdan, courtesy name Ziwen; at seven he was like an adult and was chosen as Renzong's study companion.
translations.idiomatic: Zongdan, courtesy name Ziwen, was precocious at seven and was chosen as Emperor Renzong's study companion.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，獲超選，為?從所詆，上書言狀，帝曰：「宗旦陪朕幼學，勤勞居多，此出朕意，豈應訴以常格？」

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, he received an exceptional promotion; he was slandered by palace attendants, submitted a memorial stating the facts, and the emperor said: "Zongdan accompanied me in childhood studies and his diligent service was great; this promotion came from my own intent—how can it be challenged by ordinary rules?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor acceded, Zongdan received an exceptional promotion, but palace attendants slandered him. He submitted a memorial explaining the circumstances. The emperor said, "Zongdan studied with me from childhood and has served me diligently. This promotion was my own decision—how can it be challenged under the usual rules?"

sentences.zh: 所生母死，請別擇葬域，歲時奠祀，後遂著為法。

translations.literal: When his birth mother died, he requested that a separate burial ground be chosen and seasonal offerings made; this later became established law.
translations.idiomatic: When his birth mother died, he asked that a separate burial site be chosen and seasonal sacrifices performed there. This practice later became established precedent.

sentences.zh: 治平中，同知大宗正事。

translations.literal: In the Zhiping era he served as Associate Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhiping he served as Associate Director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，拜崇信軍節度使、同中書門下平章事，為大宗正，賜方團金帶，非朝會得乘肩輿。

translations.literal: When Shenzong took the throne, he was appointed Military Commissioner of Chongxin and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, made Grand Director of the Imperial Clan Court, granted a square gold belt with round plaques, and permitted a shoulder-borne carriage outside court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong acceded, he was made Military Commissioner of Chongxin and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, appointed Grand Director of the Imperial Clan Court, granted a square gold belt with round plaques, and allowed a shoulder-borne carriage when not attending court.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，封華陰郡王，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huayin Commandery and given the honorific Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng he was enfeoffed Prince of Huayin and granted the honorific Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 長屬籍十六年

translations.literal: He long headed the clan register for sixteen years
translations.idiomatic: He headed the clan register for sixteen years

sentences.zh: 〈「長屬籍十六年」：按《長編》卷三二三載神宗詔，謂「宗旦嘗侍仁宗講讀，其後典司宗籍十有六年」，與此處事正合。

translations.literal: 〈On "headed the clan register for sixteen years": According to Comprehensive Chronicle juan 323, recording Shenzong's edict, it says "Zongdan once attended Renzong in lectures and reading; afterward he presided over the clan register for fully sixteen years," which matches this passage.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note on "headed the clan register for sixteen years": The Comprehensive Chronicle, juan 323, records an edict of Emperor Shenzong stating that "Zongdan once attended Emperor Renzong in lectures and reading, and afterward presided over the clan register for fully sixteen years," which agrees with this passage.

sentences.zh: 《宋會要》職官二○之五，謂「序同姓之親而第其五屬之戚疏者為屬籍」。

translations.literal: Song Huiyao, Offices 20.5, states: "Ordering kinsmen of the same surname and ranking the closeness or distance of the five degrees of mourning constitutes the clan register."
translations.idiomatic: The Song Huiyao (Offices 20.5) defines the clan register as "the ordering of same-surname kinsmen and the ranking of closeness and distance within the five degrees of mourning."

sentences.zh: 「宗籍」當即「屬籍」。

translations.literal: "Clan register" should be the same as "kin register."
translations.idiomatic: "Clan register" here should be understood as "kin register."

sentences.zh: 此處「籍」字原作「疾」，據改。〉

translations.literal: Here the character for "register" was originally "illness"; emended accordingly.〉
translations.idiomatic: Here the character for "register" originally read "illness" and has been emended accordingly.〉

sentences.zh: ，宗子有過，優游誨導，一善必以聞。

translations.literal: , when clansmen erred he patiently instructed and guided them, and any good deed he was sure to report.
translations.idiomatic: When members of the clan fell short, he patiently instructed them, and whenever one did well he was sure to report it.

sentences.zh: 異時赴朝請者，率以私丁給侍，宗旦建請，始得從官給。

translations.literal: In former times those who came to court for audiences were generally supplied attendants from private households; Zongdan memorialized, and only then were they supplied from official allocations.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, clansmen attending court had generally been supplied with attendants from their private households. Zongdan memorialized on the matter, and only then were they supplied from official allocations.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太尉、滕王，謚恭孝，聽旗節印綬從葬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Grand Marshal and Prince of Teng, posthumous title Gongxiao, permitted banners, insignia, seals, and ribbons to accompany the burial.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Prince of Teng, with the posthumous title Respectful and Filial, and was granted banners, insignia, seals, and ribbons for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 宗悌字元發，輕財好施。

translations.literal: Zongti, courtesy name Yuanfa; he was light with wealth and fond of giving.
translations.idiomatic: Zongti, courtesy name Yuanfa, was free with his wealth and generous in giving.

sentences.zh: 故相王氏子持父所服帶求質錢，宗悌惻然曰：「宰相子亦至是乎！」

translations.literal: A son of the former chief minister Wang brought his father's belt to pawn for money; Zongti said with compassion: "Even a chief minister's son has come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: A son of the former chief minister Wang brought his father's belt to pawn for cash. Zongti said with pity, "Even a chief minister's son has come to this!"

sentences.zh: 歸帶而與之錢。

translations.literal: He returned the belt and gave him money.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the belt and gave him the money.

sentences.zh: 所親用詐取藏鏹，得其狀，曰：「吾不以小故傷骨肉恩。」

translations.literal: A close associate used deception to take hidden treasure; when he learned the facts, he said: "I will not let a small matter wound the bond of flesh and blood."
translations.idiomatic: A close kinsman used deception to take hidden treasure. When Zongti learned of it, he said, "I will not let a small matter wound the bond of kinship."

sentences.zh: 竟不問。

translations.literal: In the end he did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 所生母早世，宗悌不識也，聞父婢語平生，輒掩泣。

translations.literal: His birth mother died early; Zongti never knew her, but when he heard his father's maidservants speak of her life he would cover his face and weep.
translations.idiomatic: His birth mother had died young, and Zongti never knew her, yet when he heard his father's maidservants speak of her life he would cover his face and weep.

sentences.zh: 繼得其肖貌，繪而奉之如生。

translations.literal: Later he obtained her likeness, painted it, and honored it as though she were alive.
translations.idiomatic: Later he obtained her likeness, had it painted, and venerated the portrait as though she were still alive.

sentences.zh: 終明州觀察使，贈保寧軍節度使、同中書門下平章事、東陽郡王，謚曰孝憲。

translations.literal: He ended as Commissioner of Mingzhou; posthumously made Military Commissioner of Baoning, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Prince of Dongyang Commandery; posthumous title Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Commissioner of Mingzhou and was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Baoning, Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Prince of Dongyang, with the posthumous title Filial and Magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 宗惠，封魏國公，尋以旁支黜。

translations.literal: Zonghui was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei, but soon removed as a collateral line.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui was enfeoffed Duke of Wei but was soon removed because he came from a collateral line.

sentences.zh: 終武昌軍節度觀察留後、江夏郡王，贈郯王。

translations.literal: He ended as Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Wuchang and Prince of Jiangxia Commandery; posthumously made Prince of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Wuchang and Prince of Jiangxia, and was posthumously made Prince of Tan.

sentences.zh: 允言，累官左屯衞將軍。

translations.literal: Yunyuan, cumulatively to General of the Left Encampment Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyuan rose to the post of General of the Left Encampment Guards.

sentences.zh: 嘗託疾不朝，降太子左衞率府率，歲中復官，又坐笞侍婢，而兄允升勸止，悖慢無禮，貶副率，絕朝謁，出之別第。

translations.literal: He once feigned illness and did not attend court, was demoted to Commandant of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent's Household, within the year restored to office; again, for beating a maidservant while his elder brother Yunsheng tried to stop him, he was insolent and disrespectful, demoted to Deputy Commandant, barred from court audiences, and sent out to a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: He once feigned illness to avoid court, was demoted to Commandant of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent's Household, and was restored within the year. Later, for beating a maidservant while his elder brother Yunsheng tried to restrain him, he answered with insolence and disrespect, was demoted to Deputy Commandant, barred from court audiences, and sent to a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 以祀汾陰恩，復率府率，還宮。

translations.literal: Through the grace of the Fengyin sacrifice he was restored as Commandant of the Guards Household and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Through the grace granted on the Fengyin sacrifice he was restored as Commandant of the Guards Household and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，復朝謁，歷左監門衞大將軍、黃州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while he was again permitted court audiences, and served as Grand General of the Left Gate Guards and Prefect of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again allowed to attend court and served as Grand General of the Left Gate Guards and Prefect of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 天聖七年卒，贈明州觀察使、奉化侯。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Tiansheng; posthumously made Commissioner of Mingzhou and Marquis of Fenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Tiansheng and was posthumously made Commissioner of Mingzhou and Marquis of Fenghua.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，贈安遠軍節度使，追封密國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao he was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Anyuan and retroactively enfeoffed as Duke of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao he was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Anyuan and retroactively enfeoffed Duke of Mi.

sentences.zh: 子宗說、宗立事並見上。

translations.literal: Sons Zongshuo and Zongli—their affairs are both recorded above.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zongshuo and Zongli are both treated above.

sentences.zh: 宗育，終右屯衞將車，贈潁州防禦使、汝陰侯。

translations.literal: Zongyu ended as General of the Right Encampment Guards; posthumously made Defender of Yingzhou and Marquis of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyu ended as General of the Right Encampment Guards and was posthumously made Defender of Yingzhou and Marquis of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 允成，終右神武將軍、濮州防禦使，贈安化軍節度使、郇國公。

translations.literal: Yuncheng ended as General of the Right Divine Martial Guards and Defender of Puzhou; posthumously made Military Commissioner of Anhua and Duke of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Yuncheng ended as General of the Right Divine Martial Guards and Defender of Puzhou and was posthumously made Military Commissioner of Anhua and Duke of Xun.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，加贈鎮江軍節度使兼侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao he was further posthumously made Military Commissioner of Zhenjiang and Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao he was further posthumously made Military Commissioner of Zhenjiang and Concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子宗顏、宗訥、宗鼎、宗嚴、宗魯、宗儒、宗奭，皆為環?、刺史。

translations.literal: Sons Zongyan, Zongne, Zongding, Zongyan, Zonglu, Zongru, and Zongshi—all were [prefects of] Huan[zhou] and regional prefects.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zongyan, Zongne, Zongding, Zongyan, Zonglu, Zongru, and Zongshi all served as prefects of Huanzhou and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 昭成太子元僖

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Zhaocheng Yuanxi
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Zhaocheng Yuanxi

sentences.zh: 昭成太子元僖，初名德明。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Zhaocheng Yuanxi, original name Deming.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Zhaocheng Yuanxi, whose original name was Deming.

sentences.zh: 太平興國七年出閤，授檢校太保、同平章事，封廣平郡王，與兄衞王德崇同日受封。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo he left the inner quarters, was appointed Grand Guardian by inspection and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping Commandery, and on the same day as his elder brother Prince of Wei Dechong received enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo he left the inner quarters, was appointed honorary Grand Guardian and concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, enfeoffed Prince of Guangping, and received his title on the same day as his elder brother Dechong, Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 八年，進封陳王，改名元佑。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was advanced to Prince of Chen and renamed Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was advanced to Prince of Chen and given the name Yuanyou.

sentences.zh: 詔自今宰相班宜在親王上，宰相宋琪、李昉請遵舊制，不允。

translations.literal: An edict declared that from now on chief ministers' court ranks should stand above imperial princes'; chief ministers Song Qi and Li Fang asked to follow the old regulations; it was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that henceforth chief ministers should rank above imperial princes at court. Chief Ministers Song Qi and Li Fang asked to follow the old regulations, but the emperor did not approve.

sentences.zh: 宋琪等懇請久之，上曰：「宰相之任，實總百揆，與羣司禮絕；

translations.literal: Song Qi and others earnestly pleaded for a long while; the emperor said: "The office of chief minister truly oversees the hundred duties and is ceremonially set apart from all other offices;
translations.idiomatic: Song Qi and the others pleaded at length. The emperor said, "The chief minister's charge truly oversees all government, and his ceremonial standing is set apart from every other office;

sentences.zh: 藩邸之設，止奉朝請而已。

translations.literal: the establishment of princely residences is only to attend court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: princely establishments exist only to attend court audiences.

sentences.zh: 元佐等尚幼，欲其知謙損之道，卿等無固讓也。」

translations.literal: Yuanzuo and the others are still young; I wish them to know the way of humility and restraint—you ministers need not insist on yielding."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzuo and the others are still young, and I wish them to learn humility and restraint. You ministers need not insist on yielding."

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，元佐被疾，以元僖為開封尹兼侍中，改今名，進封許王，加中書令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, when Yuanzuo fell ill, Yuanxi was made Prefect of Kaifeng and Concurrent Palace Attendant, given his present name, advanced to Prince of Xu, and given the additional title of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi, when Yuanzuo fell ill, Yuanxi was made Prefect of Kaifeng and Concurrent Palace Attendant, given his present name, advanced to Prince of Xu, and appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上為娶隰州團練使李謙溥女為夫人，因謂宰相曰：「朕嘗語諸子，今姻偶皆將相大臣之家，六禮具備，得不自重乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor arranged his marriage to the daughter of Li Qianpu, Regimentation Commissioner of Xizhou, as his consort, and thereupon said to the chief ministers: "I once told my sons that now their marriage partners are all from families of generals and chief ministers, with the six rites fully observed—should they not hold themselves in high regard?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor arranged his marriage to the daughter of Li Qianpu, Regimentation Commissioner of Xizhou, as his consort, and told the chief ministers, "I once told my sons that their marriages would now be to families of generals and chief ministers, with the six rites fully observed—should they not conduct themselves with proper dignity?"

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，宰相呂蒙正復上言，乞班諸王下，詔不允。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, Chief Minister Lü Mengzheng again memorialized, asking to rank below the princes; an edict did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunhua, Chief Minister Lü Mengzheng again memorialized asking to rank below the princes, but an edict refused.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月己亥，元僖早入朝，方坐殿廬中，覺體中不佳，徑歸府。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, day jihai, of the third year, Yuanxi entered court early; just as he was sitting in the hall antechamber he felt unwell in his body and went straight back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the eleventh month of the third year, Yuanxi came to court early. While sitting in the hall antechamber he felt unwell and went straight home.

sentences.zh: 車駕遽臨視，疾已亟，上呼之猶能應，少頃遂薨。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage hastened to visit him; the illness was already acute; the emperor called to him and he could still answer; shortly thereafter he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hurried to visit him, but the illness was already grave. The emperor called to him and he could still answer, yet within moments he was dead.

sentences.zh: 上哭之慟，廢朝五日，贈皇太子，謚恭孝。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him bitterly, suspended court for five days, posthumously made him Crown Prince, posthumous title Gongxiao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply, suspended court for five days, posthumously named him Crown Prince, and gave him the posthumous title Respectful and Filial.

sentences.zh: 元僖姿貌雄毅，沈靜寡言，尹京五年，政事無失。

translations.literal: Yuanxi's bearing was bold and resolute; he was calm and taciturn; as Prefect of the Capital for five years, in government affairs there was no lapse.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi was imposing and resolute in bearing, calm and sparing of speech. During five years as Prefect of the Capital, his administration was without fault.

sentences.zh: 及薨，上追念不已，悲泣達旦不寐，作思亡子詩示近臣。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor could not cease recalling him, wept in grief until dawn without sleep, and composed a poem mourning his dead son to show his close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the emperor could not stop thinking of him, wept until dawn without sleeping, and composed a poem mourning his lost son, which he showed to his close ministers.

sentences.zh: 宗保生二歲，母抱以入見章獻后，后留與處。

translations.literal: When Zongbao was two, his mother carried him in to see Empress Zhangxian; the empress kept him to live with her.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbao was two, his mother brought him to see Empress Zhangxian, and the empress kept him to live at court.

sentences.zh: 宗保七歲，授左侍禁，帝親為巾其首。

translations.literal: At seven Zongbao was appointed Left Palace Attendant; the emperor personally tied the cap on his head.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he was appointed Left Palace Attendant, and the emperor personally tied on his cap.

sentences.zh: 久之，歸本宮，詔朔望出入禁省。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned to his own palace; an edict permitted him to enter and leave the Forbidden Bureau on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he returned to his own residence, with permission to enter and leave the inner palace on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 累官代州防禦使，襲封燕國公。

translations.literal: He rose in office to Defender of Daizhou and succeeded to the enfeoffment as Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Defender of Daizhou and succeeded to the enfeoffment as Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 性仁恕，主藏吏盜米至千斛，貰不問。

translations.literal: By nature he was humane and forgiving; when the granary clerk stole rice up to a thousand bushels, he pardoned and did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: He was humane and forgiving by nature. When a granary clerk stole as much as a thousand bushels of rice, he pardoned the man and did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 嘗書「忍」字於座右以為戒。

translations.literal: He once wrote the character for "forbearance" at his seat as a warning to himself.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote the character for "forbearance" at his desk to remind himself.

sentences.zh: 熙寧七年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Xining.

sentences.zh: 神宗臨奠，其子仲鞠泣曰：「先臣幼養宮中，終身不自言。」

translations.literal: Shenzong attended the mourning; his son Zhongju wept and said: "My late father was reared in the palace from childhood and never spoke of it all his life."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong attended the mourning. His son Zhongju wept and said, "My late father was raised in the palace from childhood, yet he never spoke of it in his whole life."

sentences.zh: 帝感悼，遂優贈靜難軍節度使、新平郡王，謚恭靜。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved and grieved, and thereupon generously posthumously made him Military Commissioner of Jingnan and Prince of Xinping Commandery, posthumous title Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and posthumously made him Military Commissioner of Jingnan and Prince of Xinping, with the posthumous title Respectful and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 仲鞠亦好學能詩，事親居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Zhongju also loved learning and could compose poetry; in serving his parents and observing mourning he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju also loved learning and wrote poetry, and was known for filial devotion in serving his parents and observing mourning.

sentences.zh: 宗保卒，子仲恕嗣，官至忠州團練使，謚純僖。

translations.literal: When Zongbao died, his son Zhongshu succeeded; he reached office as Regimentation Commissioner of Zhongzhou, posthumous title Chunxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbao died, his son Zhongshu succeeded him, rose to Regimentation Commissioner of Zhongzhou, and received the posthumous title Pure and Joyful.

sentences.zh: 子士盉嗣。

translations.literal: Son Shisun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shisun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 商王元份

translations.literal: Prince of Shang Yuanfen
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shang Yuanfen

sentences.zh: 元份寬厚，言動中禮，標望偉如，娶崇儀使李漢斌之女。

translations.literal: Yuanfen was generous and magnanimous; in speech and conduct he hit the mark of ritual; his bearing was lofty and imposing; he married the daughter of Li Hanbin, Commissioner of Honored Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfen was generous and magnanimous, measured in speech and conduct, and imposing in bearing. He married the daughter of Li Hanbin, Commissioner of Honored Rites.

sentences.zh: 李悍妬慘酷，宮中女婢小不如意，必加鞭杖，或致死。

translations.literal: Li was fierce, jealous, and cruelly harsh; palace maidservants who fell slightly short of her wishes were invariably flogged, sometimes to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was fierce, jealous, and cruel. Palace maidservants who displeased her even slightly were invariably beaten, sometimes to death.

sentences.zh: 上每有恩賜，詔令均給，李盡取之。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor had gracious gifts, an edict ordered equal distribution, but Li took them all.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor granted favors, an edict ordered them shared equally, but Lady Li took everything.

sentences.zh: 及元份臥病，上親臨問，見左右無侍者，因輟宮人為主湯劑。

translations.literal: When Yuanfen lay ill, the emperor personally visited him; seeing no attendants at his side, he therefore detached palace women to prepare his medicines.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanfen fell ill, the emperor visited him in person. Finding no attendants at his side, he assigned palace women to prepare his medicines.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗崩，戚里皆赴禁中，朝晡臨，李多稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Taizong died, the imperial affines all went to the Forbidden Palace for morning and evening mourning attendance; Li often claimed illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, the imperial affines all came to the Forbidden Palace for morning and evening mourning, but Lady Li often claimed illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 元份生日，李以衣服器用為壽，皆飾以龍鳳。

translations.literal: On Yuanfen's birthday, Li presented clothes and utensils as birthday gifts, all ornamented with dragons and phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: On Yuanfen's birthday, Lady Li presented clothes and utensils as gifts, all ornamented with dragons and phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 居元份喪，無戚容，而有謗上之語。

translations.literal: During Yuanfen's mourning she showed no grieving countenance, and there were words slandering the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanfen's mourning she showed no sign of grief and spoke words slandering the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上盡知其所為，以元份故優容之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew fully what she did, but for Yuanfen's sake treated her with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew all she had done but treated her with forbearance for Yuanfen's sake.

sentences.zh: 及是，復不欲顯究其罪狀，止削國封，置之別所。

translations.literal: At this time, again unwilling to investigate her crimes openly, he only stripped her state enfeoffment and placed her in a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he again did not wish to investigate her crimes openly, but only stripped her of her state enfeoffment and placed her in a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 元份子三人：長允寧；

translations.literal: Yuanfen had three sons: the eldest Yunning;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfen had three sons: the eldest was Yunning;

sentences.zh: 次允懷，改允中，早卒；

translations.literal: next Yunhuai, renamed Yunzhong, who died young;
translations.idiomatic: next Yunhuai, who was renamed Yunzhong and died young;

sentences.zh: 次則濮王允讓也。

translations.literal: and third was Prince of Pu Yunrang.
translations.idiomatic: and third was Prince of Pu Yunrang.

sentences.zh: 允寧字德之，性至孝，因父感疾，恍惚失常。

translations.literal: Yunning, courtesy name Dezhi; by nature supremely filial; because his father contracted an illness, he became dazed and lost his normal bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yunning, courtesy name Dezhi, was supremely filial by nature. When his father fell ill, he became distraught and lost his composure.

sentences.zh: 既而嗜學，尤喜讀唐史，通知近朝典故，工虞世南楷法，真宗賜詩激賞之。

translations.literal: Afterward he loved learning, especially delighted in reading the History of Tang, was well informed in recent-court precedents, excelled in Yu Shinan's regular script, and Zhenzong granted him a poem in warm praise.
translations.idiomatic: He later took to learning, especially loved reading the History of Tang, was well versed in recent court precedents, and excelled in Yu Shinan's regular script. Emperor Zhenzong granted him a poem in warm praise.

sentences.zh: 又善射，嘗侍射後苑，屢破的，賜金帶器幣。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at archery; once attending archery in the rear park, he repeatedly hit the target and was granted a gold belt and ritual goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled at archery. Once, while attending the emperor at archery in the rear park, he repeatedly hit the target and was granted a gold belt and ritual goods.

sentences.zh: 初授右千牛衞將軍，四遷右武衞，歷唐州團練、潁州防禦、同州觀察使，進彰信軍節度觀察留後、武定軍節度使。

translations.literal: First appointed General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guards, four promotions to the Right Martial Guards, served as Regimentation Commissioner of Tangzhou, Defender of Yingzhou, Commissioner of Tongzhou, advanced to Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Zhangxin, and Military Commissioner of Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guards, promoted four times to the Right Martial Guards, and served as Regimentation Commissioner of Tangzhou, Defender of Yingzhou, and Commissioner of Tongzhou before advancing to Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Zhangxin and Military Commissioner of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年卒，贈太尉、信安郡王，謚僖簡。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Jingyou; posthumously made Grand Marshal and Prince of Xin'an Commandery, posthumous title Xijian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jingyou and was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Prince of Xin'an, with the posthumous title Joyful and Simple.

sentences.zh: 子宗諤、宗敏、宗孟、宗肅。

translations.literal: Sons Zong'e, Zongmin, Zongmeng, and Zongsu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zong'e, Zongmin, Zongmeng, and Zongsu.

sentences.zh: 宗肅封魯國公。

translations.literal: Zongsu was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Zongsu was enfeoffed Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 兄宗諤嘗亡寶器，意宗肅家人子竊之，宗肅曰：「吾廉，不足取信兄弟如此乎？」

translations.literal: His elder brother Zong'e once lost precious vessels and suspected a son of Zongsu's household of stealing them; Zongsu said: "I am upright—am I not worthy of my brothers' trust to this degree?"
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zong'e once lost precious vessels and suspected a member of Zongsu's household of stealing them. Zongsu said, "I am an honest man—is my integrity so slight that my brothers cannot trust me?"

sentences.zh: 立償其直。

translations.literal: He at once compensated their value.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately paid their full value in compensation.

sentences.zh: 宗諤愧不取，乃施諸僧。

translations.literal: Zong'e, ashamed, would not accept it and instead gave it to monks.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'e, ashamed, would not accept the money and gave it to monks instead.

sentences.zh: 久之器得，宗肅不復言。

translations.literal: After a long while the vessels were recovered; Zongsu never spoke of it again.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the vessels were recovered, but Zongsu never mentioned the matter again.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，終安化軍留後，以嘗從英宗入慶寧，優贈鎮海軍節度使、開府儀同三司、北海郡王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he ended as Observation Commissioner of Anhua; because he had once followed Yingzong into Qingning, he was generously posthumously made Military Commissioner of Zhenhai, Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, and Prince of Beihai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he ended as Observation Commissioner of Anhua. Because he had once accompanied Emperor Yingzong into Qingning, he was generously posthumously made Military Commissioner of Zhenhai, Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, and Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 宗敏終右千牛衞大將軍、文州刺史，贈越州觀察使、會稽侯。

translations.literal: Zongmin ended as Grand General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guards and Prefect of Wenzhou; posthumously made Commissioner of Yuezhou and Marquis of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin ended as Grand General of the Right Thousand-Ox Guards and Prefect of Wenzhou and was posthumously made Commissioner of Yuezhou and Marquis of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 頗涉書傳。

translations.literal: He was fairly versed in books and classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was fairly well read in the classics.

sentences.zh: 緣郊恩建請封所生母范氏，宗室子得封所生母，自宗敏始。

translations.literal: On the occasion of suburban grace he memorialized asking to enfeoff his birth mother, Lady Fan; that clansmen could enfeoff their birth mothers began with Zongmin.
translations.idiomatic: On the occasion of a suburban grace amnesty he memorialized asking to enfeoff his birth mother, Lady Fan. The right of clansmen to enfeoff their birth mothers began with Zongmin.

sentences.zh: 越王元傑

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Yuanjie
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Yuanjie

sentences.zh: 越文惠王元傑字明哲，初名德和。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue, Cultured and Kind, Yuanjie, courtesy name Mingzhe, original name Dehe.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjie, Prince of Yue, posthumously titled Cultured and Kind, whose courtesy name was Mingzhe and whose original name was Dehe.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年出閤，改名。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he left the inner quarters and was renamed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he left the inner quarters and received a new name.

sentences.zh: 授檢校太保、同平章事，封益王。

translations.literal: Appointed Grand Guardian by inspection and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, enfeoffed as Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed honorary Grand Guardian and concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and enfeoffed Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，加兼侍中、成都尹、劍南東西川節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he was additionally made Concurrent Palace Attendant, Prefect of Chengdu, and Military Commissioner of the Eastern and Western Circuits of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Duangong he was additionally made Concurrent Palace Attendant, Prefect of Chengdu, and Military Commissioner of the Eastern and Western Circuits of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，徙封吳王，領揚潤大都督府長史、淮南鎮江軍節度使。

translations.literal: In Chunhua he was transferred to Prince of Wu, heading Chief Administrator of the Yang-Yun Superior Prefecture and Military Commissioner of Zhenjiang in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua he was transferred to Prince of Wu, serving as Chief Administrator of the Yang-Yun Superior Prefecture and Military Commissioner of Zhenjiang in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，改揚州大都督、淮南忠正軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was changed to Superior Governor of Yangzhou and Military Commissioner of Zhongzheng in Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he was made Superior Governor of Yangzhou and Military Commissioner of Zhongzheng in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，授檢校太尉兼中書令、徐州大都督、武寧泰寧等軍節度使，改封兗王。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, he was appointed Grand Marshal by inspection and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, Superior Governor of Xuzhou, Military Commissioner of Wuning, Taining, and other armies, and transferred to Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded, he was appointed honorary Grand Marshal and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat, Superior Governor of Xuzhou, and Military Commissioner of Wuning, Taining, and other armies, and was transferred to Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，再郊祀，皆為終獻，加守太保。

translations.literal: In Xianping, at two suburban sacrifices he served as final presenter and was given the honorific Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping, at two suburban sacrifices he served as final presenter and was granted the honorific Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 六年七月暴薨，年三十二。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year he died suddenly, age thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year he died suddenly at the age of thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 元傑穎悟好學，善屬詞，工草、隸、飛白，建樓貯書二萬卷，及為亭榭遊息之所。

translations.literal: Yuanjie was quick-witted and loved learning, skilled at literary composition, accomplished in cursive, clerical, and flying-white scripts; he built a tower storing twenty thousand scrolls of books, and pavilions and terraces for recreation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjie was quick-witted and loved learning, skilled at literary composition, and accomplished in cursive, clerical, and flying-white calligraphy. He built a tower housing twenty thousand scrolls and pavilions and terraces for recreation.

sentences.zh: 嘗作假山，既成，置酒召僚屬觀之。

translations.literal: He once made an artificial mountain; when it was finished, he set out wine and summoned his staff to view it.
translations.idiomatic: He once built an artificial mountain, and when it was finished he set out wine and summoned his staff to view it.

sentences.zh: 翊善姚坦獨頫首不視，元傑強之，坦曰：「坦見血山，安得假山。」

translations.literal: Instructor Yao Tan alone bowed his head and would not look; Yuanjie pressed him; Tan said: "Tan sees a mountain of blood—how can there be an artificial mountain?"
translations.idiomatic: Instructor Yao Tan alone bowed his head and would not look. When Yuanjie pressed him, Tan said, "I see a mountain of blood—how can there be an artificial mountain?"

sentences.zh: 言州縣鞭撻微民，以取租稅，假山實租稅所為耳。

translations.literal: He meant that prefectures and counties flogged the common people to collect rent and tax—the artificial mountain was in truth made from rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: He meant that prefectures and counties beat the common people to collect rent and taxes—the artificial mountain was really built from those taxes.

sentences.zh: 語見姚坦傳中。

translations.literal: The words are recorded in Yao Tan's biography.
translations.idiomatic: His words are recorded in the biography of Yao Tan.

sentences.zh: 宗望字子國，終右武衞大將軍、舒州防禦使，贈安化軍節度使觀察留後、高密郡公。

translations.literal: Zongwang, courtesy name Ziguo; he ended as Grand General of the Right Martial Guards and Defender of Shuzhou; posthumously made Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Anhua and Duke of Gaomi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang, courtesy name Ziguo, ended as Grand General of the Right Martial Guards and Defender of Shuzhou and was posthumously made Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Anhua and Duke of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘗御延和殿試宗子書，以宗望為第一；

translations.literal: Renzong once held an imperial examination of clansmen's calligraphy in the Yanhe Hall, ranking Zongwang first;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong once held an imperial examination of clansmen's calligraphy in the Yanhe Hall and ranked Zongwang first;

sentences.zh: 又常獻所為文，賜國子監書，及以塗金紋羅御書「好學樂善」四字賜之。

translations.literal: he also often presented writings he had composed; he was granted books from the Directorate of Education, and the emperor wrote in his own hand on gilded patterned silk the four characters "Loves learning, delights in goodness" and granted them to him.
translations.idiomatic: he often presented his own writings and was granted books from the Directorate of Education, as well as gilded patterned silk bearing the emperor's own hand, with the four characters "Loves learning, delights in goodness."

sentences.zh: 即所居建御書閣，帝為題其榜。

translations.literal: At his residence he built an Imperial Writings Pavilion, and the emperor inscribed its plaque.
translations.idiomatic: At his residence he built an Imperial Writings Pavilion, and the emperor inscribed its plaque.

sentences.zh: 子仲郃嗣。

translations.literal: Son Zhonghe succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhonghe succeeded.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，與商恭靖王孫宗肅等同日封陳國公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, on the same day as Zongsu, grandson of the Respectful and Tranquil Prince of Shang, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining he was enfeoffed Duke of Chen on the same day as Zongsu, grandson of the Respectful and Tranquil Prince of Shang.

sentences.zh: 官至陳州觀察使。

translations.literal: He reached office as Commissioner of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Commissioner of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚良僖。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Liangxi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he received the posthumous title Good and Joyful.

sentences.zh: 鎮王元偓

translations.literal: Prince of Zhen Yuanwei
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhen Yuanwei

sentences.zh: 鎮恭懿王元偓字希道。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhen, Respectful and Virtuous, Yuanwei, courtesy name Xidao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanwei, Prince of Zhen, posthumously titled Respectful and Virtuous, whose courtesy name was Xidao.

sentences.zh: 端拱元年出閤，授檢校太保、左衞上將軍，封徐國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duangong he left the inner quarters, was appointed Grand Guardian by inspection and General of the Left Guards, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duangong he left the inner quarters, was appointed honorary Grand Guardian and General of the Left Guards, and enfeoffed Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，拜洪州都督、鎮南軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was appointed Governor-General of Hongzhou and Military Commissioner of Zhennan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he was appointed Governor-General of Hongzhou and Military Commissioner of Zhennan.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加同平章事，封彭城郡王。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, he was given Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded, he was made concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and enfeoffed Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 俄加檢校太傅，改鎮靜難、彰化，進封寧王。

translations.literal: Shortly he was given Grand Tutor by inspection, transferred to command Jingnan and Zhanghua, and advanced to Prince of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made honorary Grand Tutor, transferred to command Jingnan and Zhanghua, and advanced to Prince of Ning.

sentences.zh: 郊祀、東封，悉為亞獻，禮成，授檢校太尉兼侍中、護國鎮國等軍節度。

translations.literal: At suburban sacrifice and the eastern feng, he served throughout as secondary presenter; when the rites were completed, he was appointed Grand Marshal by inspection and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and Military Commissioner of Huguo, Zhenguo, and other armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice and the eastern feng he served as secondary presenter throughout. When the rites were completed, he was appointed honorary Grand Marshal and Concurrent Palace Attendant and made Military Commissioner of Huguo, Zhenguo, and other armies.

sentences.zh: 三年，文武官詣闕請祠后土，元偓以領節帥亦奏章以請，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the third year, civil and military officials went to court requesting sacrifice to Earth, and Yuanwei, as a commander holding the seal, also memorialized to request it; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year civil and military officials came to court requesting sacrifice to Earth. Yuanwei, as a frontier commander, also memorialized to join the rite, and an edict approved.

sentences.zh: 將行，命為河、華管內橋道頓遞使。

translations.literal: Before departure he was appointed Commissioner for Bridges, Roads, and Relay Stations within the He and Hua circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Before the journey he was appointed Commissioner for Bridges, Roads, and Relay Stations within the He and Hua circuits.

sentences.zh: 明年，車駕入境，元偓奏方物、酒餼、金帛、茗藥為貢，儀物甚盛。

translations.literal: The next year, when the imperial carriage entered his territory, Yuanwei presented local products, wine and dried meats, gold and silk, tea and medicines as tribute; the ritual goods were very lavish.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the imperial procession entered his territory, Yuanwei presented local products, wine and provisions, gold and silk, tea and medicines as tribute, with very lavish ceremonial display.

sentences.zh: 至河中，與判府陳堯叟分導乘輿度蒲津橋。

translations.literal: At Hezhong he and Chen Yaosou, Administrator of the Prefecture, together guided the imperial carriage across the Pu Ford Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: At Hezhong he and Chen Yaosou, Administrator of the Prefecture, together guided the imperial carriage across the Pu Ford Bridge.

sentences.zh: 上登鄈丘亭，目元偓曰：「橋道頓置嚴謹，爾之力也。」

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the Zouqiu Pavilion, looked at Yuanwei, and said: "The bridges, roads, and relay stations were set up with strict care—this is your doing."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the Zouqiu Pavilion, looked at Yuanwei, and said, "The bridges, roads, and relay stations were arranged with great care—this is your doing."

sentences.zh: 元偓頓首謝。

translations.literal: Yuanwei kowtowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanwei kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 及還，加中書令，領成德、安國等軍節度，改封相王。

translations.literal: On returning, he was given Director of the Secretariat, commanded Chengde, Anguo, and other armies, and transferred to Prince of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey he was made Director of the Secretariat, given command of Chengde, Anguo, and other armies, and transferred to Prince of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 五年，加守太傅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given the honorific Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was granted the honorific Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 真宗自即位以來，屢以學術勗宗子。

translations.literal: From the time Zhenzong took the throne, he repeatedly urged the clansmen with learning and the arts.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he acceded, Emperor Zhenzong repeatedly urged the clansmen to pursue learning and the arts.

sentences.zh: 元偓首冠藩戚，益自修勵，上每製篇什，必令屬和。

translations.literal: Yuanwei stood first among the imperial kin and redoubled his self-cultivation; whenever the emperor composed a piece, he was sure to have him harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanwei stood foremost among the imperial kin and redoubled his efforts at self-cultivation. Whenever the emperor composed a poem, he had Yuanwei supply a matching verse.

sentences.zh: 一日，謂宰相曰：「朕每戒宗子作詩習射，如聞頗精習，將臨觀焉。」

translations.literal: One day he said to the chief ministers: "I constantly admonish the clansmen to compose poetry and practice archery; I hear they have become quite skilled and intend to observe them in person."
translations.idiomatic: One day he told the chief ministers, "I constantly urge the clansmen to compose poetry and practice archery. I hear they have become quite skilled, and I intend to observe them myself."

sentences.zh: 因幸元偓邸第，宴從官，宮僚畢會，賦七言詩。

translations.literal: Thereupon he visited Yuanwei's residence, feasted the attending officials, gathered all palace staff, and composed heptasyllabic poems.
translations.idiomatic: He then visited Yuanwei's residence, feasted the attending officials, gathered all the palace staff, and had them compose heptasyllabic poems.

sentences.zh: 元偓奉觴上壽，賜襲衣、金帶、器幣、緡錢，又與宗室射于西南亭。

translations.literal: Yuanwei raised his cup to offer longevity; he was granted court robes, a gold belt, ritual goods, and strings of cash; he also shot with the clan at the Southwest Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanwei raised his cup to offer birthday wishes and was granted court robes, a gold belt, ritual goods, and strings of cash. He also shot with the clan at the Southwest Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 日晡，從官退，上獨以中官從，幸元偁、元儼宮，復宴元偓宮，如家人禮，夜二鼓而罷。

translations.literal: At sundown the attending officials withdrew; the emperor alone, with eunuchs in attendance, visited the palaces of Yuancheng and Yuanyan, then again feasted at Yuanwei's palace with the etiquette of family, dispersing at the second watch of night.
translations.idiomatic: At sundown the attending officials withdrew. The emperor went alone with eunuchs in attendance to visit the palaces of Yuancheng and Yuanyan, then feasted again at Yuanwei's palace with the informality of family, and did not disperse until the second watch of night.

sentences.zh: 六年，進位太尉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was advanced to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was advanced to Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，以榮王宮火，徙元偓宮於景龍門外，車駕臨幸。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year, because the Prince of Rong's palace caught fire, Yuanwei's palace was moved outside the Jinglong Gate, and the imperial carriage visited.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year, when the Prince of Rong's palace caught fire, Yuanwei's palace was moved outside the Jinglong Gate, and the emperor visited in person.

sentences.zh: 是冬，加兼尚書令。

translations.literal: That winter he was additionally made Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was additionally made Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年二月，換成德、鎮寧二鎮，進封徐王。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Tianxi he was transferred to the two commands of Chengde and Zhenning and advanced to Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Tianxi he was transferred to the commands of Chengde and Zhenning and advanced to Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 二年春，宮邸遺燼，燔舍數區，元偓驚悸，暴中風眩薨，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, a stray ember in the palace residence burned several compounds; Yuanwei was shocked and alarmed, suddenly struck by wind dizziness, and died, age forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year a stray ember in the palace residence burned several buildings. Yuanwei was shocked and alarmed, suddenly stricken with apoplexy, and died at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 帝臨哭，廢朝五日，贈太師、尚書令、鄧王，賜謚恭懿。

translations.literal: The emperor attended the mourning, suspended court for five days, posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Prince of Deng, and granted the posthumous title Gongyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor attended the mourning, suspended court for five days, posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Prince of Deng, and granted the posthumous title Respectful and Virtuous.

sentences.zh: 元偓姿表偉異，厚重寡言，曉音律。

translations.literal: Yuanwei's appearance was imposing and unusual; he was weighty and taciturn, and understood musical pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanwei was imposing and unusual in appearance, weighty and sparing of speech, and understood musical pitch.

sentences.zh: 後改封密王，又改王蘇。

translations.literal: Later his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Mi, then again to Prince of Su.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was changed to Prince of Mi, and then again to Prince of Su.

sentences.zh: 治平中，追封韓王。

translations.literal: In Zhiping he was retroactively enfeoffed as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhiping he was retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 子允弼，八歲召入禁中，令皇子致拜，允弼不敢當。

translations.literal: Son Yunbi, at eight summoned into the Forbidden Palace; the emperor ordered the imperial princes to bow to him, but Yunbi did not dare accept it.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yunbi was summoned into the Forbidden Palace at the age of eight. The emperor ordered the imperial princes to bow to him, but Yunbi did not dare accept.

sentences.zh: 御樓觀酺，得與王子並坐

translations.literal: Viewing the communal feast from the imperial tower, he was permitted to sit alongside the princes
translations.idiomatic: When viewing the communal feast from the imperial tower, he was permitted to sit alongside the princes

sentences.zh: 〈「得與王子並坐」：按上下文，「王子」當作「皇子」。〉

translations.literal: 〈On "permitted to sit alongside the princes": according to the context, "princes" should read "imperial princes."〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note on "permitted to sit alongside the princes": according to the context, "princes" should read "imperial princes."〉

sentences.zh: 皇子即位，是為仁宗。

translations.literal: The imperial prince acceded to the throne; this was Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial prince acceded to the throne, and this was Emperor Renzong.

sentences.zh: 允弼累遷武寧軍節度使兼侍中，判大宗正事，封北海郡王。

translations.literal: Yunbi was repeatedly transferred to Military Commissioner of Wuning and Concurrent Palace Attendant, served as Concurrent Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Beihai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yunbi rose through successive appointments to Military Commissioner of Wuning and Concurrent Palace Attendant, served concurrently as director of the Imperial Clan Court, and was enfeoffed Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 英宗時，拜中書令，徙王東平。

translations.literal: In the time of Yingzong, he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and transferred to Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yingzong he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and transferred to Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，拜太保、鳳翔雄武軍節度使，朝朔望。

translations.literal: When Shenzong took the throne, he was appointed Grand Guardian and Military Commissioner of Fengxiang and Xiongwu, attending court on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong acceded, he was appointed Grand Guardian and Military Commissioner of Fengxiang and Xiongwu, and attended court on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年，丁母憂，悲痛不勝喪，固辭起復。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xining, he entered mourning for his mother; grief overwhelmed him beyond what the mourning rites could bear, and he firmly declined recall from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xining he entered mourning for his mother. Grief overwhelmed him beyond what mourning could contain, and he firmly declined to be recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 母葬有日而允弼病篤，顧諸子以不得終大事為恨。

translations.literal: The day of his mother's burial was at hand, but Yunbi was critically ill; he looked upon his sons and regretted that he could not see the rites through to the end.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's burial was imminent, but Yunbi was critically ill. He looked upon his sons and lamented that he would not be able to see the rites through to the end.

sentences.zh: 薨，帝臨哭之慟，輟朝三日，贈太師、尚書令兼中書令，追封相王，謚孝定。

translations.literal: He died; the emperor attended the mourning in deep grief, suspended court for three days, posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, retroactively enfeoffed him as Prince of Xiang, and granted the posthumous title Xiaoding.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor attended the mourning in deep grief and suspended court for three days. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Xiang, and granted the posthumous title Filial and Stable.

sentences.zh: 允弼性端重，時然後言。

translations.literal: Yunbi's nature was dignified and weighty; he spoke only when the time was right.
translations.idiomatic: Yunbi was dignified and weighty by nature, and spoke only when the occasion called for it.

sentences.zh: 諸宮增學官員，允弼已貴，猶日至講席，延伴讀官讀孟子一節。

translations.literal: When the various palaces increased their study staff, though Yunbi was already exalted, he still went daily to the lecture seat and invited the co-reader to read one section of Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: When the various palaces increased their study staffs, Yunbi, though already of high rank, still went daily to the lecture hall and had the co-reader read one section of the Mencius.

sentences.zh: 領宗正三十年，與濮安懿王共事，相友愛，為宗屬推敬。

translations.literal: He headed the Imperial Clan Court for thirty years, served together with the Respectful and Virtuous Prince of Pu, and they were mutually affectionate; the clansmen held them in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: He headed the Imperial Clan Court for thirty years and worked alongside the Respectful and Virtuous Prince of Pu in mutual affection, and the clansmen held them both in reverence.

sentences.zh: 子宗繢，襲祖恭懿王封為韓國公。

translations.literal: Son Zonghui inherited his grandfather's enfeoffment as Respectful and Virtuous and was made Duke of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zonghui inherited his grandfather's Respectful and Virtuous enfeoffment and was made Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈南康郡王，謚良孝。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Prince of Nankang Commandery; posthumous title Liangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Prince of Nankang and granted the posthumous title Good and Filial.

sentences.zh: 宗繢弟宗景，以相州觀察使同知大宗正事。

translations.literal: Zonghui's younger brother Zongjing served as Commissioner of Xiangzhou and Concurrent Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui's younger brother Zongjing served as Commissioner of Xiangzhou and concurrent vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 神宗以其父允弼司宗久，故復選用之。

translations.literal: Shenzong, because his father Yunbi had long administered the clan court, again selected and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong, because his father Yunbi had long administered the Imperial Clan Court, again selected him for service.

sentences.zh: 宗景事母孝，居喪如不能勝。

translations.literal: Zongjing was filial toward his mother; in mourning he seemed unable to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Zongjing was filial toward his mother, and in mourning he seemed unable to bear the grief.

sentences.zh: 居第火冒，急赴家廟，不恤其他，火亦不為害。

translations.literal: When fire broke out at his residence, he rushed to the family temple without regard for anything else, and the fire did not harm it.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out at his residence, he rushed to the family temple without regard for anything else, and the fire did not harm it.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，累遷彰德軍節度、開府儀同三司、檢校司空，封濟陰郡王。

translations.literal: In the Yuanyou era he was repeatedly transferred to Military Commissioner of Zhangde, Grand Preceptor of the Privy with the Three Excellencies, and Honorary Minister of Works, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiyin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou he rose through successive appointments to Military Commissioner of Zhangde, Grand Preceptor of the Privy with the Three Excellencies, and Honorary Minister of Works, and was enfeoffed Prince of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 宗景喪其夫人，將以妾繼室，先出之於外，而託為良家女且納焉。

translations.literal: When Zongjing lost his wife and planned to install a concubine as successor, he first sent her away and then, passing her off as a respectable family's daughter, took her in.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongjing lost his wife and planned to make a concubine his new primary consort, he first sent her away and then, falsely presenting her as a respectable family's daughter, took her in.

sentences.zh: 坐奪開府，既而還之。

translations.literal: For this he was stripped of his Grand Preceptor of the Privy title, but it was restored shortly afterward.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was stripped of his Grand Preceptor of the Privy title, but it was restored shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年薨，年六十六，贈太師、循王，謚曰思。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng he died, age sixty-six; posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Prince of Xun; posthumous title Si.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaosheng he died at the age of sixty-six. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Prince of Xun and granted the posthumous title Reflective.

sentences.zh: 宗繢既卒，子仲嗣，自平川節度使徙劍南西川。

translations.literal: After Zonghui died, his son Zhongsi, from Military Commissioner of Pingchuan was transferred to Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Zonghui died, his son Zhongsi was transferred from Military Commissioner of Pingchuan to Military Commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 徽宗改封韓王為鎮王。

translations.literal: Huizong changed the enfeoffment of Prince of Han to Prince of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong changed the title of Prince of Han to Prince of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 楚王元偁

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Yuancheng
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chu Yuancheng

sentences.zh: 先是，諸王子授官，即為諸?將軍，餘以父官及族屬親疏差等。

translations.literal: Previously, when various princes received appointments, they were immediately made various guard generals; the rest differed according to their fathers' offices and the closeness or distance of kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when imperial princes received appointments, they were immediately made various guard generals; other appointments varied according to their fathers' rank and the closeness of kinship.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，令宗正卿趙安仁議為定制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi, the emperor ordered Director of the Imperial Clan Court Zhao Anren to deliberate and establish a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi the emperor ordered Zhao Anren, director of the Imperial Clan Court, to deliberate and establish a fixed regulation.

sentences.zh: 安仁請以宣祖、太祖、太宗孫初廕授將軍，曾孫授右侍禁，玄孫授右班殿直，內父爵高者聽從高廕，其事緣特旨者不以為例。

translations.literal: Anren requested that grandsons of Xuanzu, Taizu, and Taizong at first yin enfeoffment be made generals; great-grandsons receive Right Attendant-in-Waiting; great-great-grandsons receive Right Ban Palace Attendant; within these, if the father's rank was higher, they were permitted to follow the higher yin; matters arising from special edicts were not taken as precedent.
