translations.idiomatic: Anren proposed that grandsons of Xuanzu, Taizu, and Taizong at first inherited enfeoffment be made generals; great-grandsons, Right Attendant-in-Waiting; great-great-grandsons, Right Ban Palace Attendant. Where the father's rank was higher, they might follow the higher inherited appointment; cases arising from special edicts would not be taken as precedent.

sentences.zh: 詔中書、門下、樞密院參定行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Secretariat-Chancellery and Privy Council to consult, determine, and implement it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Secretariat-Chancellery and the Privy Council to consult, determine, and implement it.

sentences.zh: 周王元儼

translations.literal: Prince of Zhou Yuanyan
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhou Yuanyan

sentences.zh: 周恭肅王元儼，少奇穎，太宗特愛之。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhou, Respectful and Solemn, Yuanyan, was quick-witted and outstanding from youth; Taizong especially loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyan, Prince of Zhou, posthumously titled Respectful and Solemn, was exceptionally bright from youth, and Emperor Taizong loved him especially.

sentences.zh: 每朝會宴集，多侍左右。

translations.literal: At every court assembly and feast he mostly attended at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: At every court assembly and feast he mostly attended at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 帝不欲元儼早出宮，期以年二十始就封，故宮中稱為「二十八太保」，蓋元儼於兄弟中行第八也。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish Yuanyan to leave the palace early; he planned that enfeoffment would begin only at age twenty, so within the palace he was called the "Twenty-Eighth Grand Guardian"—for Yuanyan ranked eighth among his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish Yuanyan to leave the palace early and planned that he would receive his enfeoffment only at age twenty, so within the palace he was called the "Twenty-Eighth Grand Guardian"—because Yuanyan ranked eighth among his brothers.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，授檢校太保、左衞上將軍，封曹國公。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne, he was appointed Grand Guardian by inspection and General of the Left Guards, and enfeoffed as Duke of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded, he was appointed honorary Grand Guardian and General of the Left Guards and enfeoffed Duke of Cao.

sentences.zh: 明年，為平海軍節度使，拜同中書門下平章事，加檢校太傅，封廣陵郡王。

translations.literal: The next year he became Military Commissioner of Pinghai, was appointed Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, given Grand Tutor by inspection, and enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became Military Commissioner of Pinghai, was appointed Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, made honorary Grand Tutor, and enfeoffed Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，改昭武、安德軍節度使，進封榮王；

translations.literal: At the feng of Mount Tai, he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Zhaowu and Ande and advanced to Prince of Rong;
translations.idiomatic: At the feng of Mount Tai he was transferred to Military Commissioner of Zhaowu and Ande and advanced to Prince of Rong;

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，加兼侍中，改鎮安靜、武信，加檢校太尉；

translations.literal: at the sacrifice at Fenyin, he was additionally made Concurrent Palace Attendant, transferred to Anjing and Wuxin, and given Grand Marshal by inspection;
translations.idiomatic: at the sacrifice at Fenyin he was additionally made Concurrent Palace Attendant, transferred to command Anjing and Wuxin, and made honorary Grand Marshal;

sentences.zh: 祠太清宮，加兼中書令。

translations.literal: at the rites at the Temple of the Supreme Ultimate, he was additionally made Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: at the rites at the Temple of the Supreme Ultimate he was additionally made Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 坐侍婢縱火，延燔禁中，奪武信節，降封端王，出居故駙馬都尉石保吉第。

translations.literal: Because a serving maid set a fire that spread and burned the Forbidden Palace, his Wuxin command was stripped, he was demoted and enfeoffed as Prince of Duan, and moved out to the former residence of the late Grand Master of the Empress's Equipage, Shi Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: Because a serving maid set a fire that spread through the Forbidden Palace, his Wuxin command was stripped, he was demoted to Prince of Duan, and moved out to the former residence of the late Grand Master of the Empress's Equipage, Shi Baoji.

sentences.zh: 每見帝，痛自引過，帝憫憐之。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw the emperor, he bitterly blamed himself; the emperor pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw the emperor, he bitterly blamed himself, and the emperor pitied him.

sentences.zh: 尋加鎮海、安化軍節度使，封彭王，進太保。

translations.literal: Shortly he was additionally made Military Commissioner of Zhenhai and Anhua, enfeoffed as Prince of Peng, and advanced to Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was additionally made Military Commissioner of Zhenhai and Anhua, enfeoffed Prince of Peng, and advanced to Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為皇子，加太傅。

translations.literal: When Renzong was made imperial prince, he was given Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was made imperial heir, he was given the title Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 歷橫海永清保平定國節度、陝州大都督，改通王、涇王。

translations.literal: He successively held the commands of Heng-Hai, Yongqing, Baoping, and Dingguo, and was Superior Governor of Shaanzhou; his title was changed to Prince of Tong and Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He successively held the commands of Heng-Hai, Yongqing, Baoping, and Dingguo and was Superior Governor of Shaanzhou, and his title was changed to Prince of Tong and then Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，拜太尉、尚書令兼中書令，徙節鎮安、忠武，封定王，賜贊拜不名，又賜詔書不名。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, he was appointed Grand Marshal, Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, transferred to the commands of Zhen'an and Zhongwu, enfeoffed as Prince of Ding, granted praise-and-bow without speaking his name, and again granted edicts without speaking his name.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he was appointed Grand Marshal, Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, transferred to the commands of Zhen'an and Zhongwu, enfeoffed Prince of Ding, granted the privilege of praise and bow without the speaking of his name, and again granted edicts that omitted his name.

sentences.zh: 天聖七年，封鎮王，又賜劍履上殿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tiansheng he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhen, and again granted sword and shoes in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tiansheng he was enfeoffed Prince of Zhen and again granted the privilege of wearing sword and shoes in the imperial hall.

sentences.zh: 明道初，拜太師，換河陽三城、武成節度，封孟王，改永興鳳翔、京兆尹，封荊王，遷雍州、鳳翔牧。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingdao he was appointed Grand Preceptor, transferred to the commands of Heyang Sancheng and Wucheng, enfeoffed as Prince of Meng, changed to Yong-Xing, Fengxiang, and Mayor of Jingzhao, enfeoffed as Prince of Jing, and transferred to Governor of Yongzhou and Prefect of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Mingdao he was appointed Grand Preceptor, transferred to the commands of Heyang Sancheng and Wucheng, enfeoffed Prince of Meng, then given Yong-Xing, Fengxiang, and the mayoralty of Jingzhao, enfeoffed Prince of Jing, and made Governor of Yongzhou and Prefect of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 景祐二年大封拜宗室，授荊南、淮南節度大使荊南淮南節度大使，行荊州、揚州牧，仍賜入朝不趨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou, at the great enfeoffment of the imperial clan, he was appointed Grand Military Commissioner of Jingnan and Huainan, Grand Military Commissioner of Jingnan and Huainan, acting Governor of Jingzhou and Yangzhou, and was again granted that when entering court he need not hasten his pace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyou, at the great enfeoffment of the imperial clan, he was appointed Grand Military Commissioner of Jingnan and Huainan, Grand Military Commissioner of Jingnan and Huainan, acting Governor of Jingzhou and Yangzhou, and was again granted that when entering court he need not hasten his pace.

sentences.zh: 元儼廣顙豐頤，嚴毅不可犯，天下崇憚之，名聞外夷，事母王德妃孝，妃每有疾，躬侍藥，晨夕盥潔焚香以禱，至憂念不食。

translations.literal: Yuanyan had a broad forehead and full cheeks; stern and formidable, he could not be violated; the empire revered and feared him, and his name reached foreign tribes. He was filial toward his mother, the Virtuous Consort Wang; whenever the consort fell ill, he personally attended her medicine, morning and evening washed himself and burned incense to pray, and in utmost worry and thought went without food.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyan had a broad forehead and full cheeks. Stern and formidable, he could not be crossed; the empire revered and feared him, and his fame reached foreign tribes. He was filial toward his mother, the Virtuous Consort Wang: whenever she fell ill, he personally attended her medicine, washed himself morning and evening and burned incense in prayer, and in his anxiety went without food.

sentences.zh: 母喪，哀戚過人。

translations.literal: At his mother's mourning, his grief exceeded others'.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's mourning, his grief exceeded that of others.

sentences.zh: 平生寡嗜慾，惟喜聚書，好為文詞，頗善二王書，工飛白。

translations.literal: All his life he had few desires; he only delighted in gathering books, loved composing literary pieces, was quite skilled at the script of the Two Wangs, and was accomplished at flying-white calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he had few desires and delighted only in gathering books. He loved composing literary pieces, was quite skilled at the script of the Two Wangs, and was accomplished at flying-white calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 仁宗年即位，章獻皇后臨朝，自以屬尊望重，恐為太后所忌，深自沉晦。

translations.literal: When Renzong acceded in youth, Empress Zhangxian held court; he considered himself high in kinship rank and heavy in prestige, feared the empress dowager would be jealous, and deeply concealed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded while still young, Empress Dowager Zhangxian held court. Considering himself high in kinship rank and heavy in prestige, he feared the empress dowager would be jealous and deeply lowered his profile.

sentences.zh: 因闔門卻絕人事，故謬語陽狂，不復預朝謁。

translations.literal: Therefore he shut his gates and cut off contact with people, deliberately spoke absurdities and feigned madness, and no longer attended court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his gates and cut off contact with the world, deliberately spoke absurdities and feigned madness, and no longer attended court audiences.

sentences.zh: 及太后崩，仁宗親政，益加尊寵，凡有請報可，必手書謝牘。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died and Renzong personally governed, favor toward him increased still more; whenever there was a petition granted approval, he invariably wrote a thank-you note in his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager died and Emperor Renzong personally governed, he was honored still more. Whenever a petition of his was granted approval, he invariably wrote a thank-you note in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 方陝西用兵，上所給公用錢歲五十萬以助邊費，帝不欲拒之，聽入其半。

translations.literal: At the time when war was being waged in Shaanxi, the court each year granted him five hundred thousand in public funds to assist border expenses; the emperor did not wish to refuse him and permitted him to accept half.
translations.idiomatic: While war was being waged in Shaanxi, the court each year granted him five hundred thousand in public funds to assist border expenses. The emperor did not wish to refuse him outright and permitted him to accept half.

sentences.zh: 嘗問翊善王渙曰：「元昊平未？」

translations.literal: He once asked Instructor Wang Huan: "Has Yuanhao been pacified yet?"
translations.idiomatic: He once asked Instructor Wang Huan, "Has Yuanhao been pacified yet?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「未也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Not yet."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan replied, "Not yet.

sentences.zh: 曰：「如此，安用宰相為。」

translations.literal: He said: "If that is so, what use are chief ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyan said, "If that is so, what use are chief ministers?

sentences.zh: 聞者畏其言。

translations.literal: Those who heard his words feared them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard his words were intimidated by them.

sentences.zh: 子十三人：允熙、允良、允迪、允初，餘皆早卒。

translations.literal: He had thirteen sons: Yunxi, Yunliang, Yundi, and Yunchu; the rest all died early.
translations.idiomatic: He had thirteen sons: Yunxi, Yunliang, Yundi, and Yunchu survived; the rest all died early.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，以允良子宗絳嗣封吳國公。

translations.literal: In Xining, Yunliang's son Zongjiang was appointed successor and enfeoffed as Duke of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: During Xining, Yunliang's son Zongjiang was appointed successor and enfeoffed Duke of Wu.

sentences.zh: 徽宗改封吳王為周王。

translations.literal: Huizong changed the enfeoffment of Prince of Wu to Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong changed the title of Prince of Wu to Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 允熙終右監門衞將軍、滁州刺史，贈博州防禦使、博平侯。

translations.literal: Yunxi ended as General of the Right Gate Guards and Prefect of Chuzhou; posthumously made Defender of Bozhou and Marquis of Boping.
translations.idiomatic: Yunxi ended as General of the Right Gate Guards and Prefect of Chuzhou and was posthumously made Defender of Bozhou and Marquis of Boping.

sentences.zh: 允良歷五節度，領寧海、平江兩軍，封華原郡王，改襄陽，由同中書門下平章事、兼侍中，至太保、中書令。

translations.literal: Yunliang successively held five commands, headed Ninghai and Pingjiang, was enfeoffed as Prince of Huayuan Commandery, transferred to Xiangyang, rose from Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Concurrent Palace Attendant to Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Yunliang successively held five commands, headed Ninghai and Pingjiang, was enfeoffed Prince of Huayuan, transferred to Xiangyang, and rose from Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Concurrent Palace Attendant to Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 好酣寢，以日為夜，由是一宮之人皆晝睡夕興。

translations.literal: He loved deep sleep, taking day for night; from this the entire palace household slept by day and rose at night.
translations.idiomatic: He loved deep sleep and took day for night, so the entire palace household came to sleep by day and rise at night.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈定王，有司以其反易晦明，謚曰榮易。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Prince of Ding; the office considered that he had reversed light and dark, and granted the posthumous title Rongyi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Prince of Ding. The office considered that he had reversed light and dark and granted the posthumous title Rongyi.

sentences.zh: 允迪累官耀州觀察使。

translations.literal: Yundi rose through offices to Commissioner of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yundi rose through offices to Commissioner of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 居父喪不哀，又嘗宮中為優戲，為妻昭國夫人錢氏所告。

translations.literal: In his father's mourning he showed no grief; he also once performed comic entertainment in the palace and was reported by his wife, the Lady of Zhaoguo, née Qian.
translations.idiomatic: During his father's mourning he showed no grief, and he once performed comic entertainment in the palace and was reported by his wife, the Lady of Zhaoguo, née Qian.

sentences.zh: 制降右監門衞大將軍，絕朝謁，錢氏亦度為洞真道士。

translations.literal: By decree he was demoted to Grand General of the Right Gate Guards, barred from court audiences, and Lady Qian was also ordained a Taoist priest of Dongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: By decree he was demoted to Grand General of the Right Gate Guards and barred from court audiences, and Lady Qian was also ordained a Taoist priest of Dongzhen.

sentences.zh: 允初，初名允宗，勤於朝會，雖風雨不廢。

translations.literal: Yunchu, originally named Yunzong, was diligent in court assemblies; even in wind and rain he did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchu, originally named Yunzong, was diligent in court assemblies and did not cease even in wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 未嘗問財物厚薄，惟誦佛書，人以為不慧。

translations.literal: He never inquired into the abundance or scarcity of wealth; he only recited Buddhist books, and people considered him not clever.
translations.idiomatic: He never inquired into the abundance or scarcity of wealth and only recited Buddhist texts; people considered him not clever.

sentences.zh: 累遷寧國軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Military Commissioner of Ningguo and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Military Commissioner of Ningguo and Concurrent Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 治平元年卒，贈中書令、博平郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiping he died; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Prince of Boping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiping he died and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Prince of Boping.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 英宗臨奠，以允初後事屬其兄允良，乃以允成孫仲連為之後。

translations.literal: Yingzong attended the mourning; he entrusted Yunchu's later affairs to his elder brother Yunliang, and so Yuncheng's grandson Zhonglian was made his successor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong attended the mourning, entrusted Yunchu's later affairs to his elder brother Yunliang, and made Yuncheng's grandson Zhonglian his successor.

sentences.zh: 崇王元億

translations.literal: Prince of Chong Yuanyi
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chong Yuanyi

sentences.zh: 崇王元億，早亡，追賜名，封代國公。

translations.literal: Prince of Chong Yuanyi died early; posthumously granted a name and enfeoffed as Duke of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi, Prince of Chong, died early; a name was posthumously granted and he was enfeoffed Duke of Dai.

sentences.zh: 治平中，封安定郡王。

translations.literal: In Zhiping he was enfeoffed as Prince of Anding Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhiping he was enfeoffed Prince of Anding.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，加封崇王。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne, his enfeoffment was increased to Prince of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong acceded, his enfeoffment was increased to Prince of Chong.

sentences.zh: 真宗六子：長溫王禔，次悼獻太子祐，次昌王祗，次信王祉，次欽王祈，次仁宗。

translations.literal: Zhenzong had six sons: the eldest was Prince of Wen Ti; next Heir Apparent Daoxian You; next Prince of Chang Di; next Prince of Xin Zhi; next Prince of Qin Qi; next Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong had six sons: the eldest was Prince of Wen Ti; next came Heir Apparent Daoxian You; then Prince of Chang Di; then Prince of Xin Zhi; then Prince of Qin Qi; and lastly Renzong.

sentences.zh: 禔、祗、祈皆蚤亡，徽宗賜名追封。

translations.literal: Ti, Di, and Qi all died early; Huizong posthumously granted names and enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: Ti, Di, and Qi all died early; Emperor Huizong posthumously granted names and enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 悼獻太子祐，母曰章穆皇后。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Daoxian You—his mother was Empress Zhangmu.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Daoxian You's mother was Empress Zhangmu.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，封信國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he was enfeoffed Duke of Xin.

sentences.zh: 生九年而薨，追封周王，賜謚悼獻。

translations.literal: He lived nine years and died; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhou and granted the posthumous title Daoxian.
translations.idiomatic: He lived nine years and died; he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Zhou and granted the posthumous title Daoxian.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，贈太尉、中書令。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，追冊皇太子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao he was retroactively enfeoffed as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao he was retroactively enfeoffed Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 悼獻太子祐

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Daoxian You
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Daoxian You

sentences.zh: 真宗六子：長溫王禔，次悼獻太子祐，次昌王祗，次信王祉，次欽王祈，次仁宗。

translations.literal: Zhenzong had six sons: the eldest was Prince of Wen Ti; next Heir Apparent Daoxian You; next Prince of Chang Di; next Prince of Xin Zhi; next Prince of Qin Qi; next Renzong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong had six sons: the eldest was Prince of Wen Ti; next came Heir Apparent Daoxian You; then Prince of Chang Di; then Prince of Xin Zhi; then Prince of Qin Qi; and lastly Renzong.

sentences.zh: 禔、祗、祈皆蚤亡，徽宗賜名追封。

translations.literal: Ti, Di, and Qi all died early; Huizong posthumously granted names and enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: Ti, Di, and Qi all died early; Emperor Huizong posthumously granted names and enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 悼獻太子祐，母曰章穆皇后。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Daoxian You—his mother was Empress Zhangmu.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Daoxian You's mother was Empress Zhangmu.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，封信國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he was enfeoffed Duke of Xin.

sentences.zh: 生九年而薨，追封周王，賜謚悼獻。

translations.literal: He lived nine years and died; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhou and granted the posthumous title Daoxian.
translations.idiomatic: He lived nine years and died; he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Zhou and granted the posthumous title Daoxian.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，贈太尉、中書令。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 明道二年，追冊皇太子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingdao he was retroactively enfeoffed as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingdao he was retroactively enfeoffed Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 濮王允讓

translations.literal: Prince of Pu Yunrang
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pu Yunrang

sentences.zh: 仁宗三子：長楊王昉，次雍王昕，次荊王曦，皆早亡。

translations.literal: Renzong had three sons: the eldest was Prince of Yang Fang; next Prince of Yong Xin; next Prince of Jing Xi; all died early.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong had three sons: the eldest was Prince of Yang Fang; next Prince of Yong Xin; next Prince of Jing Xi; all died early.

sentences.zh: 徽宗時改封。

translations.literal: In the time of Huizong the enfeoffments were changed.
translations.idiomatic: During Huizong's reign the enfeoffments were changed.

sentences.zh: 濮安懿王允讓字益之，商王元份子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Pu, Respectful and Virtuous, Yunrang, courtesy name Yizhi, was a son of Prince of Shang Yuanfen.
translations.idiomatic: Yunrang, Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Respectful and Virtuous, whose courtesy name was Yizhi, was a son of Prince of Shang Yuanfen.

sentences.zh: 天資渾厚，外莊內寬，喜慍不見于色。

translations.literal: His natural endowment was solid and deep; outwardly stern yet inwardly generous; joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He was solid and deep by nature, outwardly stern yet inwardly generous, and neither joy nor anger showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 始為右千將軍。

translations.literal: He first served as Right Thousand General.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Right Thousand-Ox General.

sentences.zh: 周王祐薨，真宗以綠車旄節迎養于禁中。

translations.literal: When Prince of Zhou You died, Zhenzong welcomed and raised him in the Forbidden Palace with a green carriage and plumed banners.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Zhou You died, Emperor Zhenzong welcomed him into the Forbidden Palace to be raised there, with a green carriage and plumed banners.

sentences.zh: 仁宗生，用簫韶部樂送還邸。

translations.literal: When Renzong was born, he was sent back to his residence with the music of the Xiao and Shao repertoire.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was born, he was sent back to his residence with the court music of the Xiao and Shao repertoire.

sentences.zh: 官衞州刺史。

translations.literal: He held office as Prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，授汝州防禦使，累拜寧江軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, he was appointed Defender-in-Chief of Ruzhou; over time he was promoted to Military Commissioner of the Ningjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded, he was appointed Defender-in-Chief of Ruzhou and, over time, was promoted to Military Commissioner of the Ningjiang Army.

sentences.zh: 上建睦親宅，命知大宗正寺。

translations.literal: The emperor built the Muqin Residence and ordered him to serve as Director of the Grand Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor built the Muqin Residence for harmonious kinship, he was ordered to direct the Grand Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 宗子有好學，勉進之以善，若不率教，則勸戒之，至不變，始正其罪，故人莫不畏服焉。

translations.literal: Among clansmen who loved learning he encouraged them toward virtue; if they did not follow instruction he admonished them; only when they would not change did he formally punish their offenses. Therefore no one failed to respect and submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: When clansmen showed a love of learning, he urged them toward what was good; if they would not heed instruction, he admonished them; only when they remained unchanged did he formally punish their offenses. For this reason everyone respected and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 慶曆四年，封汝南郡王，拜同平章事，改判大宗正司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qingli he was enfeoffed Prince of Runan Commandery, appointed Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and transferred to serve as Concurrent Director of the Grand Imperial Clan Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qingli he was enfeoffed Prince of Runan Commandery, appointed Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and transferred to serve concurrently as Director of the Grand Imperial Clan Office.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐四年薨，年六十五，贈太尉、中書令，追封濮王，謚安懿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiayou he died, aged sixty-five; posthumously made Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Pu, posthumous title Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiayou he died at sixty-five; he was posthumously made Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Pu, and granted the posthumous title Anyi.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在位久無子，乃以王第十三子宗實為皇子。

translations.literal: Renzong had long been on the throne without a son; thereupon the Prince's thirteenth son Zongshi was made Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong had long reigned without a son, so the Prince's thirteenth son, Zongshi, was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 仁宗崩，皇子即位，是為英宗。

translations.literal: When Renzong died, the Crown Prince succeeded to the throne; this was Yingzong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong died, the crown prince succeeded to the throne; this was Emperor Yingzong.

sentences.zh: 治平元年，宰相韓琦等奏：請下有司議濮安懿王及譙國夫人王氏、襄國夫人韓氏、仙遊縣君任氏合行典禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiping, Chancellor Han Qi and others memorialized: requesting that relevant offices be ordered to deliberate on the appropriate rites for Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, Lady Wang of Qiao State, Lady Han of Xiang State, and Lady Ren, Lady of Xianyou County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiping, Chancellor Han Qi and others memorialized, asking that the relevant offices be instructed to deliberate on the proper rites for Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, Lady Wang of Qiao State, Lady Han of Xiang State, and Lady Ren, Lady of Xianyou County.

sentences.zh: 詔須大祥後議之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the matter be debated after the major mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the matter be debated only after the major mourning period had been completed.

sentences.zh: 二年，乃詔禮官與待制以上議。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered rites officials and those of Attending-Drafter rank and above to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, an edict ordered the rites officials and all officials of Attending-Drafter rank and above to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士王珪等奏曰：謹按儀禮喪服：「為人後者」傳曰：「何以三年也？

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others memorialized: We respectfully cite the Ceremonies and Rites, Mourning Dress: "One who becomes another's heir" — the commentary says: "Why three years?
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others memorialized: "We respectfully cite the Ceremonies and Rites, Mourning Dress: 'One who becomes another's heir' — the commentary asks, 'Why three years?

sentences.zh: 受重者必以尊服服之。」

translations.literal: One who receives the weight of succession must wear the highest mourning garments."
translations.idiomatic: One who receives the weight of succession must wear the highest grade of mourning."

sentences.zh: 「為所後者之祖父母妻，妻之父母昆弟，昆弟之子若子。」

translations.literal: For the grandparents, wife, wife's parents, brothers, and brothers' sons of the one to whom one succeeds, [one mourns] as for one's own sons."
translations.idiomatic: For the grandparents, wife, wife's parents, brothers, and brothers' sons of the one to whom one succeeds, one mourns as for one's own sons."

sentences.zh: 謂皆如親子也。

translations.literal: This means all are treated as one's own sons.
translations.idiomatic: This means that all are treated as one's own sons.

sentences.zh: 又「為人後者為其父母」傳曰：「何以期？

translations.literal: Further, "One who becomes another's heir [mourns] for his own parents" — the commentary says: "Why one year?
translations.idiomatic: Further: "One who becomes another's heir [mourns] for his own parents" — the commentary asks, "Why one year?

sentences.zh: 不二斬，持重於大宗，降其小宗也。」

translations.literal: One does not wear the highest grade twice; one upholds the weight of the great lineage and reduces mourning for the lesser lineage."
translations.idiomatic: One does not wear the highest mourning grade twice; one upholds the weight of the great lineage and reduces mourning for the lesser lineage."

sentences.zh: 「為人後者為其昆弟」傳曰：「何以大功？

translations.literal: One who becomes another's heir [mourns] for his own brothers" — the commentary says: "Why nine months?
translations.idiomatic: One who becomes another's heir [mourns] for his own brothers" — the commentary asks, "Why nine months?

sentences.zh: 為人後者降其昆弟也。」

translations.literal: One who becomes another's heir reduces mourning for his own brothers."
translations.idiomatic: One who becomes another's heir reduces the mourning owed to his own brothers."

sentences.zh: 先王制禮，尊無二上，若恭愛之心分於彼，則不得專於此故也。

translations.literal: The ancient kings devised rites so that there is but one supreme object of reverence; if reverent affection is divided toward that side, one cannot be devoted to this side — that is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings devised rites on the principle that reverence has but one supreme object: if reverent affection is divided toward that side, one cannot be wholly devoted to this side. That is the reason.

sentences.zh: 是以秦、漢以來，帝王有自旁支入承大統者，或推尊其父母以為帝后，皆見非當時，取議後世，臣等不敢引以為聖朝法。

translations.literal: Thus from Qin and Han onward, when emperors from collateral lines succeeded to the great succession, some promoted their own parents to Emperor and Empress — all were faulted in their own day and brought forth discussion in later ages; we your subjects dare not cite these as models for our sage dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Thus from Qin and Han onward, when emperors from collateral lines succeeded to the great succession, some elevated their own parents to Emperor and Empress — all were condemned in their own day and debated by later ages. We your subjects dare not cite such precedents as models for our sage dynasty.

sentences.zh: 况前代入繼者，多宮車晏駕之後，援立之策或出臣下，非如仁宗皇帝年齡未衰，深惟宗廟之重，祗承天地之意，於宗室眾多之中，簡推聖明，授以大業。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who succeeded from collateral lines in former dynasties mostly did so after the imperial carriage had halted at dusk; the plans to install them often came from ministers — not as when Emperor Renzong, his years not yet declined, deeply considered the weight of the ancestral temple, reverently received Heaven and Earth's intent, and from among the many in the imperial clan selected and promoted the sage and bright one, entrusting to him the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in former dynasties those who succeeded from collateral lines mostly did so only after the emperor's death, and the plans to install them often came from ministers below — nothing like the case of Emperor Renzong, whose years were not yet spent, who deeply weighed the weight of the ancestral temple, reverently received Heaven and Earth's intent, and from among the many in the imperial clan singled out the sage and bright heir and entrusted to him the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 陛下親為先帝之子，然後繼體承祧，光有天下。

translations.literal: Your Majesty became the late emperor's own son, and only then succeeded to the body of the lineage and carried forward the ancestral sacrifice, illuminating and possessing all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty became the late emperor's own son and only then succeeded to the imperial body and carried forward the ancestral sacrifice, illuminating and possessing all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 濮安懿王雖於陛下有天性之親，顧復之恩，然陛下所以負扆端冕，富有四海，子子孫孫萬世相承，皆先帝德也。

translations.literal: Though Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, had with Your Majesty the kinship of nature and the grace of nurturing, yet that Your Majesty sits at the royal screen wearing the ceremonial cap, possesses the wealth of the four seas, and that sons and grandsons will inherit for ten thousand generations — all this is the late emperor's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Though Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, bore to Your Majesty the kinship of nature and the grace of nurturing, yet that Your Majesty sits at the royal screen in ceremonial cap and robe, possesses the wealth of the four seas, and that sons and grandsons will inherit for ten thousand generations — all this is the late emperor's virtue.

sentences.zh: 臣等竊以為濮王宜準先朝封贈期親尊屬故事，尊以高官大國，譙國、襄國、仙遊並封太夫人，攷之古今為宜稱。

translations.literal: We your subjects respectfully believe the Prince of Pu should follow the precedents of former dynasties for enfeoffing and bestowing posthumous honors on close imperial relatives — honored with high office and a great fief; Qiao, Xiang, and Xianyou should all be enfeoffed Grand Madame; examining antiquity and the present, these titles are fitting.
translations.idiomatic: We your subjects respectfully believe that the Prince of Pu should follow former precedents for enfeoffing and honoring close imperial relatives — honored with high office and a great fief; the ladies of Qiao, Xiang, and Xianyou should all be enfeoffed Grand Madame. Examining antiquity and the present, these titles are fitting.

sentences.zh: 於是中書奏：王珪等所議，未見詳定濮王當稱何親，名與不名？

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat memorialized: Wang Gui and others' deliberations did not clearly determine what kinship term the Prince of Pu should bear — to name him or not?
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Secretariat memorialized that Wang Gui and others' deliberations had not clearly settled what kinship term the Prince of Pu should bear, or whether he should be named.

sentences.zh: 珪等議：「濮安於仁宗為兄，於皇帝宜稱皇伯而不名，如楚王、涇王故事。」

translations.literal: Gui and others deliberated: "Prince Pu An was elder brother to Renzong; toward the Emperor he should be styled Imperial Uncle without naming him, following the precedents of Prince of Chu and Prince of Jing."
translations.idiomatic: Gui and others argued: "Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, was elder brother to Emperor Renzong; toward the Emperor he should be styled Imperial Uncle without naming him, following the precedents of the Princes of Chu and Jing."

sentences.zh: 中書又奏：「禮與令及五服年月敕：出繼之子於所繼、所生皆稱父母。

translations.literal: The Secretariat again memorialized: "The Rites, Statutes, and the Edict on the Five Mourning Grades and durations state: a son who leaves one lineage to succeed in another calls both the one he succeeds and the one who begot him 'father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat again memorialized: "The Rites, Statutes, and the Edict on the Five Mourning Grades and their durations state that a son who leaves one lineage to succeed in another calls both the one he succeeds and the one who begot him 'father and mother.

sentences.zh: 又漢宣帝、光武皆稱父為皇考。

translations.literal: Moreover, Emperor Xuan of Han and Emperor Guangwu both styled their fathers Imperial Forefather.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Emperor Xuan of Han and Emperor Guangwu both styled their fathers "Imperial Forefather."

sentences.zh: 今珪等議稱濮王為皇伯，於典禮未有明據，請下尚書省，集三省、御史臺議奏。」

translations.literal: Now Gui and others propose styling the Prince of Pu as Imperial Uncle, for which the canonical rites have no clear warrant; we request that the matter be sent down to the Department of State Affairs, with the Three Departments and Censorate convened to deliberate and report."
translations.idiomatic: Now Gui and others propose styling the Prince of Pu as Imperial Uncle, for which the canonical rites offer no clear warrant. We request that the matter be sent to the Department of State Affairs and that the Three Departments and the Censorate be convened to deliberate and report."

sentences.zh: 方議而皇太后手詔詰責執政，於是詔曰：「如聞集議不一，權宜罷議，令有司博求典故以聞。」

translations.literal: While debate was underway, the Empress Dowager issued a handwritten edict rebuking the chief ministers; thereupon an edict said: "As I hear the assembled debates are not united, the discussions are provisionally suspended; let the relevant offices broadly seek historical precedents and report."
translations.idiomatic: While debate was still underway, the Empress Dowager issued a handwritten edict rebuking the chief ministers. Thereupon an edict said: "As I hear the assembled debates are not united, the discussions are provisionally suspended; let the relevant offices broadly seek historical precedents and report."

sentences.zh: 禮官范鎮等又奏：「漢之稱皇考、稱帝、稱皇，立寢廟，序昭穆，皆非陛下聖明之所法，宜如前議為便。」

translations.literal: Rites officials Fan Zhen and others again memorialized: "Han usages of styling Imperial Forefather, Emperor, and Imperial, establishing mortuary temples and ordering zhao and mu — none of these should be models for Your Majesty's sagely wisdom; the earlier proposal is more fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Rites officials Fan Zhen and others again memorialized: "The Han usages of styling Imperial Forefather, Emperor, and Imperial, establishing mortuary temples, and ordering zhao and mu — none of these should be models for Your Majesty's sagely wisdom. The earlier proposal is more fitting."

sentences.zh: 自是御史呂誨等彈奏歐陽脩首建邪議，韓琦、曾公亮、趙槩附會不正之罪，固請如王珪等議。

translations.literal: Thereupon censor Lu Hui and others impeached Ouyang Xiu for originating heterodox proposals, and Han Qi, Zeng Gongliang, and Zhao Kai for concurring with what was not correct; they firmly requested following Wang Gui and others' proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Censor Lu Hui and others impeached Ouyang Xiu for originating heterodox proposals, and Han Qi, Zeng Gongliang, and Zhao Kai for concurring with what was incorrect; they firmly requested that the court follow Wang Gui and others' proposal.

sentences.zh: 既而內出皇太后手詔曰：「吾聞羣臣議請皇帝封崇濮安懿王，至今未見施行。

translations.literal: Soon afterward an edict issued from within the palace by the Empress Dowager said: "I have heard the assembled ministers propose that the Emperor ennoble and honor Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, yet to this day I have not seen it carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward an edict issued from within the palace in the Empress Dowager's own hand said: "I have heard the assembled ministers propose that the Emperor ennoble and honor Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, yet to this day I have not seen this carried out.

sentences.zh: 吾載閱前史，乃知自有故事。

translations.literal: When I repeatedly examined earlier histories, I learned that precedents indeed exist.
translations.idiomatic: When I repeatedly examined earlier histories, I learned that precedents indeed exist.

sentences.zh: 濮安懿王、譙國夫人王氏、襄國夫人韓氏、仙遊縣君任氏，可令皇帝稱親，濮安懿王稱皇，王氏、韓氏、任氏並稱后。」

translations.literal: Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi; Lady Wang of Qiao State; Lady Han of Xiang State; and Lady Ren, Lady of Xianyou County — the Emperor may style them as kin; Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, may be styled Imperial; Lady Wang, Lady Han, and Lady Ren may all be styled Empress."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi; Lady Wang of Qiao State; Lady Han of Xiang State; and Lady Ren, Lady of Xianyou County — the Emperor may style them as kin; Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, may be styled Imperial; and Lady Wang, Lady Han, and Lady Ren may all be styled Empress."

sentences.zh: 事方施行，而英宗即日手詔曰：「稱親之禮，謹遵慈訓；

translations.literal: Just as the matter was to be implemented, Yingzong that same day issued a handwritten edict: "In the rites of styling kin, I respectfully follow my mother's instruction;
translations.idiomatic: Just as the matter was to be implemented, Emperor Yingzong that same day issued a handwritten edict: "In the rites of styling kin, I respectfully follow my mother's instruction;

sentences.zh: 追崇之典，豈易克當。

translations.literal: the canon of posthumous elevation — how easily could I deem myself worthy.
translations.idiomatic: but the canon of posthumous elevation — how easily could I deem myself worthy of it.

sentences.zh: 且欲以塋為園，即園立廟，俾王子孫主奉祠事。」

translations.literal: For now I wish to make the tomb enclosure a park, establish a temple within the park, and have the Prince's sons and grandsons preside over the sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: For now I wish to make the tomb enclosure a park, establish a temple within the park, and have the Prince's sons and grandsons preside over the sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 翌日，誨等以所論列彈奏不見聽用，繳納御史敕告，家居待罪。

translations.literal: The next day, Hui and others, finding their impeachment memorials not accepted, returned their censorial commissions and edicts, and remained at home awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when Hui and others found that their impeachment memorials had not been accepted, they returned their censorial commissions and edicts and remained at home awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 誨等所列，大抵以為前詔稱「權罷集議」，後詔又稱「且欲以塋為園」，即追崇之意未已。

translations.literal: What Hui and others had set forth largely held that the earlier edict spoke of "provisionally suspending the assembled debate," while the later edict also said "for now I wish to make the tomb enclosure a park" — showing the intent of posthumous elevation had not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: What Hui and others had set forth largely held that the earlier edict spoke of "provisionally suspending the assembled debate," while the later edict also said "for now I wish to make the tomb enclosure a park" — showing that the intent of posthumous elevation had not ceased.

sentences.zh: 英宗命閤門以告還之。

translations.literal: Yingzong ordered the Gatekeepers' Office to return their memorials with notification.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong ordered the Gatekeepers' Office to return their memorials with notification.

sentences.zh: 誨等力辭臺職。

translations.literal: Hui and others vigorously declined their censorial posts.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and others vigorously declined their censorial posts.

sentences.zh: 誨等既出，而濮議亦寢。

translations.literal: Once Hui and others had withdrawn, the Pu debate also lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hui and others had withdrawn, the debate over Prince of Pu also lapsed.

sentences.zh: 至神宗元豐二年，詔以濮安懿王三夫人可並稱王夫人云。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng under Shenzong, an edict declared that the three consorts of Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, might all be styled Lady of the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Shenzong, an edict declared that the three consorts of Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, might all be styled Lady of the Prince.

sentences.zh: 王二十八子。

translations.literal: The Prince had twenty-eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince had twenty-eight sons.

sentences.zh: 長宗懿，英宗時為宿州團練使，封和國公。

translations.literal: The eldest was Zongyi; under Yingzong he was Prefectural Commander of Suzhou and enfeoffed Duke of He State.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest was Zongyi; under Emperor Yingzong he served as Prefectural Commander of Suzhou and was enfeoffed Duke of He State.

sentences.zh: 神宗以宗懿濮安懿王元子，追封舒王。

translations.literal: Shenzong, because Zongyi was the eldest son of Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, retroactively enfeoffed him Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zongyi was the eldest son of Prince of Pu, posthumously titled Anyi, Emperor Shenzong retroactively enfeoffed him Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 子仲鸞，常州防禦使。

translations.literal: His son Zhongluan was Defender-in-Chief of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongluan served as Defender-in-Chief of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 父薨，諸子皆進官，獨不忍受。

translations.literal: When his father died, all the sons were promoted in rank; he alone refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, all the sons were promoted in rank, but he alone refused to accept the promotion.

sentences.zh: 喜翰墨，樂施與，九族稱賢。

translations.literal: He loved brush and ink, delighted in giving generously, and the nine degrees of kin praised his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He loved brush and ink, delighted in generous giving, and the whole clan praised his virtue.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈武康軍節度使、洋國公，謚曰良。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Military Commissioner of the Wukang Army and Duke of Yang State; posthumous title Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Military Commissioner of the Wukang Army and Duke of Yang State, with the posthumous title Liang.

sentences.zh: 仲鸞弟仲汾，幼喜書史，一讀成誦。

translations.literal: Zhongluan's younger brother Zhongfen loved books and histories from youth; after one reading he could recite them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongluan's younger brother Zhongfen loved books and histories from youth and could recite a text after reading it once.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，鄰於毀瘠。

translations.literal: During mourning for his father he nearly wasted away in grief.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father he nearly wasted away in grief.

sentences.zh: 卒官萊州防禦使，贈昭化軍節度使、榮國公。

translations.literal: He died in office as Defender-in-Chief of Laizhou; posthumously made Military Commissioner of the Zhaohua Army and Duke of Rong State.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Defender-in-Chief of Laizhou and was posthumously made Military Commissioner of the Zhaohua Army and Duke of Rong State.

sentences.zh: 次宗樸，為隴州防禦使，封岐國公。

translations.literal: Next was Zongpu, Defender-in-Chief of Longzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Qi State.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Zongpu, who served as Defender-in-Chief of Longzhou and was enfeoffed Duke of Qi State.

sentences.zh: 宗樸與英宗友愛。

translations.literal: Zongpu and Yingzong were friendly and affectionate.
translations.idiomatic: Zongpu and Emperor Yingzong were friendly and affectionate.

sentences.zh: 初，詔英宗入居慶寧宮，固辭，宗樸率近屬敦勸，乃入。

translations.literal: At first, when an edict ordered Yingzong to move into Qingning Palace, he firmly declined; Zongpu led close kin in earnest urging, and only then did he enter.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when an edict ordered Emperor Yingzong to move into Qingning Palace, he firmly declined; Zongpu led close kin in earnest urging, and only then did he enter.

sentences.zh: 治平中，建濮王園廟，宗樸遂拜彰德軍節度使，封濮國公，奉王後。

translations.literal: In the Zhiping era, when the Prince of Pu's park temple was built, Zongpu was appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhangde Army, enfeoffed Duke of Pu State, and charged with maintaining the Prince's line.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping era, when the park temple of Prince of Pu was built, Zongpu was appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhangde Army, enfeoffed Duke of Pu State, and charged with maintaining the Prince's line.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，加同平章事兼侍中，進封濮陽郡王。

translations.literal: When Shenzong acceded, he was made Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Concurrent Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong acceded, he was made Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and was advanced to Prince of Puyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太師、中書令，追封定王，謚僖穆。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Ding, posthumous title Ximu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Ding, with the posthumous title Ximu.

sentences.zh: 子仲佺，父歿，不食者數日。

translations.literal: His son Zhongquan, when his father died, went several days without eating.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongquan went several days without eating when his father died.

sentences.zh: 母葬時，天大雪，步泥中扶翼，道路歎惻。

translations.literal: When his mother was buried, snow fell heavily; he walked through mud to support the bier, and travelers on the road sighed in sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother was buried, heavy snow was falling; he walked through mud to support the bier, and travelers on the road sighed in sympathy.

sentences.zh: 以潤州觀察使卒，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He died as Observation Commissioner of Runzhou; posthumously made Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Observation Commissioner of Runzhou and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 宗樸既薨，宗誼襲封。

translations.literal: After Zongpu died, Zongyi inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongpu died, Zongyi inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 官至昭化軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He rose to Military Commissioner of the Zhaohua Army and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Military Commissioner of the Zhaohua Army and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太師、中書令、廣陵郡王，謚莊孝。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Prince of Guangling Commandery; posthumous title Zhuangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and Prince of Guangling Commandery, with the posthumous title Zhuangxiao.

sentences.zh: 宗暉，元豐中，以淮康軍節度使襲濮國公。

translations.literal: Zonghui, in the Yuanfeng era, as Military Commissioner of the Huaikang Army inherited Duke of Pu State.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghui, in the Yuanfeng era, inherited the title Duke of Pu State while serving as Military Commissioner of the Huaikang Army.

sentences.zh: 安懿王及三夫人改祔，命為誌并題神主，加同中書門下平章事、開府儀同三司，進嗣濮王。

translations.literal: When Prince Anyi and the three consorts were re-enshrined, he was ordered to compose the epitaph and inscribe the spirit tablets; made Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies; advanced to Hereditary Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Anyi and the three consorts were re-enshrined, he was ordered to compose the epitaph and inscribe the spirit tablets; he was made Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies, and was advanced to Hereditary Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，改鎮南節度使、檢校司徒。

translations.literal: When Zhezong acceded, changed to Military Commissioner of Zhennan and Honorary Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong acceded, he was reassigned as Military Commissioner of Zhennan and Honorary Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年薨，年六十七，贈太師，追封懷王，謚榮穆。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng he died, aged sixty-seven; posthumously made Grand Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Huai, posthumous title Rongmu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaosheng he died at sixty-seven; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Huai, and granted the posthumous title Rongmu.

sentences.zh: 子仲璲。

translations.literal: His son Zhongsui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhongsui.

sentences.zh: 先是，濮國嗣王四孟詣洛享園廟，以河南府縣官充亞、終獻。

translations.literal: Previously, on the four first days of the seasons the Hereditary Prince of Pu State went to Luoyang to offer sacrifices at the park temple, with officials of Henan Prefecture and its counties serving as secondary and final presenters.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, on the four seasonal first days the Hereditary Prince of Pu State went to Luoyang to offer sacrifices at the park temple, with officials of Henan Prefecture and its counties serving as secondary and final presenters.

sentences.zh: 宗暉之襲封也，神宗始命以其子為之，仲璲遂以終獻侍祠，凡十餘年。

translations.literal: When Zonghui inherited the enfeoffment, Shenzong first ordered that his son serve in this role; Zhongsui thereupon served as final presenter at the sacrifices for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghui inherited the enfeoffment, Emperor Shenzong first ordered that his son serve in this role; Zhongsui thereupon served as final presenter at the sacrifices for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 父喪，哀痛不能勝，纔服除而卒。

translations.literal: When his father died he grieved beyond bearing; he had barely completed mourning when he died.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he grieved beyond bearing; he had barely completed mourning when he died.

sentences.zh: 官右監門衞大將軍、合州刺史。

translations.literal: He held office as Right Grand General of the Gate Guards and Prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He held office as Right Grand General of the Gate Guards and Prefect of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 宗晟，紹聖元年六月，以武安軍節度使判大宗正事，加檢校司徒，嗣濮王。

translations.literal: Zongsheng, in the sixth month of the first year of Shaosheng, as Military Commissioner of the Wu'an Army and Concurrent Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, with Honorary Minister of Education added, succeeded as Hereditary Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Zongsheng, in the sixth month of the first year of Shaosheng, succeeded as Hereditary Prince of Pu while serving as Military Commissioner of the Wu'an Army and Concurrent Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, with Honorary Minister of Education added.

sentences.zh: 明年三月薨，年六十五，贈太師、昌王，謚端孝。

translations.literal: The next year, third month, he died, aged sixty-five; posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Prince of Chang, posthumous title Duanxiao.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the third month, he died at sixty-five; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Prince of Chang, with the posthumous title Duanxiao.

sentences.zh: 宗晟好古學，藏書數萬卷，仁宗嘉之，益以國子監書。

translations.literal: Zongsheng loved classical learning; his library held tens of thousands of volumes; Renzong praised him and added books from the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Zongsheng loved classical learning and kept a library of tens of thousands of volumes; Emperor Renzong praised him and added books from the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 治平將郊而雨，或議改祫享，英宗訪諸宗晟，對曰：「陛下初郊見上帝，盛禮也，豈宜改卜。

translations.literal: When Zhiping was approaching the suburban sacrifice and rain fell, some proposed changing the date of the joint ancestral service; Yingzong consulted Zongsheng, who replied: "Your Majesty's first suburban sacrifice to appear before the Lord on High is a grand ceremony — how could the date be changed?
translations.idiomatic: As the Zhiping suburban sacrifice approached and rain fell, some proposed changing the date of the joint ancestral service; Emperor Yingzong consulted Zongsheng, who replied: "Your Majesty's first suburban sacrifice to appear before the Lord on High is a grand ceremony — how could the date be changed?

sentences.zh: 至誠感神，在陛下精意而已。」

translations.literal: Sincerity moves the spirits; everything depends on Your Majesty's devoted intent."
translations.idiomatic: Sincerity moves the spirits; everything depends on Your Majesty's devoted intent alone."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 及郊，雨霽。

translations.literal: When the suburban sacrifice came, the rain cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When the suburban sacrifice came, the rain cleared.

sentences.zh: 帝數被疾，密請早建儲貳，以係天下之望，世稱其忠。

translations.literal: The Emperor was frequently ill; he secretly pleaded for an early establishment of the heir apparent to bind the hopes of all under Heaven; the age praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was frequently ill; Zongsheng secretly pleaded for an early establishment of the heir apparent to bind the hopes of all under Heaven, and the age praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 宗晟薨，哲宗紹聖二年四月，宗愈以鎮安節度使、開府儀同三司、檢校司徒嗣封。

translations.literal: After Zongsheng died, in the fourth month of the second year of Shaosheng under Zhezong, Zongyu as Military Commissioner of Zhen'an, Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies, and Honorary Minister of Education succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongsheng died, in the fourth month of the second year of Shaosheng under Emperor Zhezong, Zongyu succeeded to the enfeoffment while serving as Military Commissioner of Zhen'an, Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies, and Honorary Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 故事嗣王以四時詣祠所，宗愈方屬疾，或曰不可以暑行，曰：「吾身主祀而不往，非禮也。」

translations.literal: By precedent the hereditary prince visits the sacrificial shrine in all four seasons; Zongyu was then afflicted with illness; some said he should not travel in the heat; he said: "I am the one charged with the sacrifices — if I do not go, that is not according to rite."
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the hereditary prince visits the sacrificial shrine in all four seasons. Zongyu was then afflicted with illness, and some said he should not travel in the heat. He said: "I am the one charged with the sacrifices — if I do not go, that is not according to rite."

sentences.zh: 強輿以行，疾遂亟。

translations.literal: He had himself carried forth by force; his illness thereupon became acute.
translations.idiomatic: He had himself carried forth by force, and his illness thereupon became acute.

sentences.zh: 是年八月薨，年六十五，贈太師，追封襄王，謚恭憲。

translations.literal: That year, eighth month, he died, aged sixty-five; posthumously made Grand Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Xiang, posthumous title Gongxian.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the eighth month, he died at sixty-five; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Xiang, and granted the posthumous title Gongxian.

sentences.zh: 宗綽嗣，官至河陽三城節度使、檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Zongchuo succeeded; he rose to Military Commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang and Honorary Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Zongchuo succeeded and rose to Military Commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang and Honorary Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 紹聖三年二月薨，年六十二，贈太師，追封榮王，謚孝靖。

translations.literal: Second month, third year of Shaosheng, he died, aged sixty-two; posthumously made Grand Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Rong, posthumous title Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year of Shaosheng he died at sixty-two; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Rong, and granted the posthumous title Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 宗祐克己自約，蕭然若寒士，好讀書，尤喜學易。

translations.literal: Zongyou restrained himself and kept to strict limits, as spare as a poor scholar; he loved reading, and especially delighted in studying the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyou restrained himself and lived sparely, like a poor scholar; he loved reading and especially delighted in studying the Changes.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，從父允初未立嗣，咸推其賢，詔以宗祐為後，泣曰：「臣不幸幼失怙恃，將終身悲慕，忍為人後乎、敢以死請。」

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era, his paternal uncle Yunchu had no established heir; all praised Zongyou's virtue; an edict made Zongyou his successor; weeping he said: "Your subject was unlucky to lose his parents in youth and will mourn them all my life — how could I bear to become another's heir? I dare request this at the cost of my life."
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiayou era, his paternal uncle Yunchu had no established heir, and all praised Zongyou's virtue. An edict made Zongyou his successor, but weeping he said: "Your subject was unlucky to lose his parents in youth and will mourn them all my life — how could I bear to become another's heir? I dare beg to refuse even at the cost of my life."

sentences.zh: 仁宗憐而從之。

translations.literal: Renzong took pity and granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong took pity and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 累遷清海軍節度使、開府儀同三司，封乘城郡王。

translations.literal: Over time he was promoted to Military Commissioner of the Qinghai Army, Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed Prince of Chengcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Over time he was promoted to Military Commissioner of the Qinghai Army and Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies, and was enfeoffed Prince of Chengcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年八月，加檢校司徒，嗣濮王。

translations.literal: August of the fourth year of Shaosheng, Honorary Minister of Education was added; he succeeded as Hereditary Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Shaosheng, Honorary Minister of Education was added, and he succeeded as Hereditary Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 時已病，當祠園廟，不肯移疾，自秋涉冬連往來。

translations.literal: He was already ill; when sacrifices at the park temple were due, he would not cite illness; from autumn through winter he traveled back and forth continually.
translations.idiomatic: He was already ill, but when sacrifices at the park temple were due he would not cite illness; from autumn through winter he traveled back and forth continually.

sentences.zh: 元符元年春，又亟往，遂薨于祠下。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Yuanfu he hurried there again and died beneath the shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Yuanfu he hurried there again and died at the shrine.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，追封欽王，謚穆恪。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Qin, posthumous title Muke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Qin, and granted the posthumous title Muke.

sentences.zh: 宗漢，英宗幼弟也。

translations.literal: Zonghan was Yingzong's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan was Emperor Yingzong's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 累拜保寧軍留後、鄴國公、東陽安康郡王。

translations.literal: Over time he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Baoning Army, Duke of Ye State, and Prince of Dongyang Anguo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Over time he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of the Baoning Army, Duke of Ye State, and Prince of Dongyang Anguo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元符初，以彰德軍節度使、開府儀同三司、檢校司空嗣濮王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfu, as Military Commissioner of the Zhangde Army, Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies, and Honorary Minister of Works, he succeeded as Hereditary Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanfu, he succeeded as Hereditary Prince of Pu while serving as Military Commissioner of the Zhangde Army, Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies, and Honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，徙寧江、保平、泰寧三鎮，判大宗正事，加檢校司徒、太保、太尉。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended the throne, [Zonghan] was transferred to the three commands of Ningjiang, Baoping, and Taining, served as Concurrent Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, and was given Honorary Minister of Education, Grand Guardian, and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Zonghan was transferred to the commands of Ningjiang, Baoping, and Taining, appointed Concurrent Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, and given the honorary titles of Minister of Education, Grand Guardian, and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 帝幸濮邸，遷其子孫官。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited the Pu residence and promoted the offices of his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor visited the residence of the Prince of Pu and promoted the offices of his descendants.

sentences.zh: 時安懿王諸子獨宗漢在，恩禮隆腆。

translations.literal: At the time, of Prince Anyi's sons only Zonghan remained, and the grace and courtesy shown him were generous and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, of Prince Anyi's sons only Zonghan still survived, and the honors and kindness accorded him were lavish and generous.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年八月薨，贈太師，追封景王，謚孝簡。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Daguan he died; posthumously made Grand Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Jing, posthumous title Xiaojian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Daguan he died; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Jing, and granted the posthumous title Xiaojian.

sentences.zh: 宗漢善畫，嘗作八鴈圖，人稱其工。

translations.literal: Zonghan was skilled at painting; he once painted Eight Geese, and people praised his artistry.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan was skilled at painting; he once painted Eight Geese, and people praised his mastery.

sentences.zh: 仲增嗣。

translations.literal: Zhongzeng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzeng succeeded to the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 仲增，濮王孫，於屬為長，故封。

translations.literal: Zhongzeng, grandson of the Prince of Pu, was eldest in the lineage, hence the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzeng, a grandson of the Prince of Pu, was the eldest in the line of succession, and therefore received the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 官至彰德軍節度使、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His offices reached Military Commissioner of the Zhangde Army and Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Military Commissioner of the Zhangde Army and Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 政和五年九月薨，贈少師，追封簡王，謚穆孝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Zhenghe he died; posthumously made Junior Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Jian, posthumous title Mu Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year of Zhenghe he died; he was posthumously made Junior Preceptor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Jian, and granted the posthumous title Mu Xiao.

sentences.zh: 仲御，自幼不羣，通經史，多識朝廷典故。

translations.literal: Zhongyu, from youth was not one of the crowd; versed in the classics and history, well acquainted with court precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyu stood apart even from childhood; he mastered the classics and histories and knew the court's precedents well.

sentences.zh: 居父宗晟喪，哲宗起知宗正，力辭，詔虛位以須終制。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his father Zongsheng, Zhezong raised him to Director of Imperial Clan Affairs; he forcefully declined, and an edict held the position vacant until mourning was complete.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father Zongsheng, Emperor Zhezong sought to appoint him Director of Imperial Clan Affairs; he forcefully declined, and an edict kept the post vacant until his mourning period was complete.

sentences.zh: 累遷鎮寧、保寧、昭信、武安節度使，封汝南、華原郡王。

translations.literal: Promoted in succession to Military Commissioner of Zhenning, Baoning, Zhaoxin, and Wu'an armies; enfeoffed Prince of Runan and Huayuan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Military Commissioner of the Zhenning, Baoning, Zhaoxin, and Wu'an armies, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Runan and Huayuan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 政和中，以檢校少傅、泰寧軍節度使、開府儀同三司嗣封。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era, as Honorary Junior Mentor, Military Commissioner of the Taining Army, and Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies, he succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe era he succeeded to the enfeoffment while serving as Honorary Junior Mentor, Military Commissioner of the Taining Army, and Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 天寧節遼使在廷，宰相適謁告，仲御攝事，率百僚上壽，若素習者。

translations.literal: On Tianning Festival a Liao envoy was at court; the chief councilor happened to be on leave for mourning; Zhongyu served in his stead, leading the hundred officials in offering longevity congratulations, as if long practiced.
translations.idiomatic: On Tianning Festival, when a Liao envoy was at court, the chief councilor happened to be on mourning leave; Zhongyu acted in his stead, leading the hundred officials in offering birthday congratulations with the ease of long practice.

sentences.zh: 帝每見必加優禮，稱為嗣王。

translations.literal: The Emperor whenever he saw him always added exceptional courtesy, calling him the Hereditary Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Emperor saw him, he treated him with special honor and called him the Hereditary Prince.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年五月薨，年七十一，贈太傅，追封郇王，謚康孝。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Xuanhe he died, aged seventy-one; posthumously made Grand Mentor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Xun, posthumous title Kang Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Xuanhe he died at seventy-one; he was posthumously made Grand Mentor, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Xun, and granted the posthumous title Kang Xiao.

sentences.zh: 仲爰嗣。

translations.literal: Zhong'ai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong'ai succeeded to the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，拜建武節度使，為大宗正，加開府儀同三司，封江夏郡王，徙節泰寧定武，檢校少保、少傅。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended the throne, [Zhong'ai] was made Military Commissioner of Jianwu, Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies, Prince of Jiangxia Commandery; transferred to command Taining and Dingwu, Honorary Junior Guardian and Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Zhong'ai was appointed Military Commissioner of Jianwu and Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, given Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangxia Commandery; he was then transferred to the commands of Taining and Dingwu and given the honorary titles of Junior Guardian and Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 宣和五年六月薨，年七十，贈太保，追封恭王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuanhe he died, aged seventy; posthumously made Grand Guardian, retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Xuanhe he died at seventy; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and retroactively enfeoffed Prince of Gong.

sentences.zh: 仲理嗣。

translations.literal: Zhongli succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli succeeded to the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，為安國軍節度使，加檢校少保、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang, he was Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army, with Honorary Junior Guardian and Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies added.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingkang era he served as Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army, with Honorary Junior Guardian and Grand Preceptor with Honorary Three Excellencies added to his titles.

sentences.zh: 嗣濮王者，英宗本生父後也。

translations.literal: The Hereditary Prince of Pu was the line of Emperor Yingzong's biological father.
translations.idiomatic: The Hereditary Prince of Pu was the line descended from Emperor Yingzong's biological father.

sentences.zh: 治平三年，立濮王園廟。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiping, the garden temple of the Prince of Pu was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiping, the garden temple of the Prince of Pu was established.

sentences.zh: 元豐七年，封王子宗暉為嗣濮王，世世不絕封。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanfeng, Prince Zun's son Zonghui was enfeoffed as Hereditary Prince of Pu, with enfeoffment to continue generation after generation without cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yuanfeng, Prince Zun's son Zonghui was enfeoffed as Hereditary Prince of Pu, with the enfeoffment to continue from generation to generation without end.

sentences.zh: 高宗南遷，奉濮王神主于紹興府光孝寺。

translations.literal: When Gaozong moved south, the spirit tablet of the Prince of Pu was installed at Guangxiao Temple in Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong moved south, the spirit tablet of the Prince of Pu was installed at Guangxiao Temple in Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 士從、士街、士籛、士衎、士歆

translations.literal: Shi Cong, Shi Jie, Shi Qian, Shi Kan, Shi Xin
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong, Shi Jie, Shi Qian, Shi Kan, and Shi Xin

sentences.zh: 子 士從、士街、士籛、士衎、士歆。

translations.literal: Sons: Shi Cong, Shi Jie, Shi Qian, Shi Kan, Shi Xin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shi Cong, Shi Jie, Shi Qian, Shi Kan, and Shi Xin.

sentences.zh: 士從，靖康末，為洺州防禦使。

translations.literal: Shi Cong, at the end of Jingkang, was Defense Commissioner of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jingkang era, Shi Cong served as Defense Commissioner of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，同知西外宗正事，主管高郵軍宗子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan, Concurrent Director of Western Outer Imperial Clan Affairs, in charge of imperial clansmen at Gaoyou Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan he served as Concurrent Director of Western Outer Imperial Clan Affairs and supervised the imperial clansmen at Gaoyou Army.

sentences.zh: 士從招潰卒置屯，奏假江、淮制置使，許之。

translations.literal: Shi Cong recruited routed soldiers and established a garrison, memorialized to borrow appointment as Jiang-Huai Commissioner for Military Affairs, and was granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong recruited routed soldiers and established a garrison, then memorialized asking to be appointed Jiang-Huai Commissioner for Military Affairs on a provisional basis; his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 賊李在犯楚州，士從遣部將乘虛掩襲，狃於小勝，軍無紀律，敗績。

translations.literal: The bandit Li Zai attacked Chuzhou; Shi Cong sent a subordinate general to strike when the enemy was exposed; complacent from a small victory, the army lacked discipline and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit Li Zai attacked Chuzhou, Shi Cong sent a subordinate commander to strike while the enemy was exposed; emboldened by a minor victory, his troops lost all discipline and were routed.

sentences.zh: 士從移司衡、溫二州。

translations.literal: Shi Cong moved his office to Heng and Wen prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong transferred his office to Heng and Wen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 臣僚以其弟士籛撓州縣，士從不能制，遂罷。

translations.literal: Officials memorialized that his younger brother Shi Qian harassed prefectures and counties and Shi Cong could not restrain him; he was thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials memorialized that his younger brother Shi Qian was harassing prefectures and counties and that Shi Cong could not control him; he was thereupon dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，遷涇、洪二州觀察使，權知濮王園令。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing, promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Jing and Hong prefectures, Acting Administrator of the Prince of Pu Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaoxing he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Jing and Hong prefectures and appointed Acting Administrator of the Prince of Pu Garden.

sentences.zh: 士從乞擇利便地奉安神位，從之。

translations.literal: Shi Cong requested permission to choose a convenient site to install the spirit seat; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Cong asked to choose a suitable site for installing the spirit seat, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 六年，士街授象州防禦使，遷華州觀察使、同知大宗正事、安慶軍承宣使，主奉濮王祠事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Shi Jie was appointed Defense Commissioner of Xiangzhou, promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Hua Prefecture, Concurrent Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, Commissioner of the Anqing Army, and charged with presiding over sacrifices to the Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Shi Jie was appointed Defense Commissioner of Xiangzhou, then promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Hua Prefecture, Concurrent Director of Imperial Clan Affairs, and Commissioner of the Anqing Army, with responsibility for presiding over sacrifices to the Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 初，以軍興，南班宗子權罷歲賜，至有身歿而不能殮者，士街言于朝，詔復舊制。

translations.literal: Earlier, because of military exigency, the annual stipends of Southern Branch imperial clansmen had been temporarily suspended, until some died without means even for burial; Shi Jie spoke to the court, and an edict restored the former practice.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because of the war, the annual stipends of Southern Branch imperial clansmen had been temporarily suspended, until some died without even the means for burial; Shi Jie appealed to the court, and an edict restored the former practice.

sentences.zh: 三十年，拜安德軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, appointed Military Commissioner of the Ande Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Ande Army.

sentences.zh: 典宗司凡十四年。

translations.literal: He presided over the Imperial Clan Bureau for fourteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Imperial Clan Bureau for fourteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 士籛官至安慶軍節度使、同知大宗正事。

translations.literal: Shi Qian's offices reached Military Commissioner of the Anqing Army and Concurrent Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qian rose to Military Commissioner of the Anqing Army and Concurrent Director of Imperial Clan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，上言：「宗司文移視官敘高下，令詪，臣兄也，位反居臣下，失尊卑敘，乞易置之。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, he memorialized: "In the Imperial Clan Bureau, documents follow official rank in precedence; Ling Xian is my elder brother, yet his rank is below mine — this reverses senior and junior and violates proper order; I beg that our positions be exchanged."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing he memorialized: "In the Imperial Clan Bureau, documents follow official rank in determining precedence. Ling Xian is my elder brother, yet his rank is below mine — this reverses senior and junior and violates proper order. I beg that our positions be exchanged."
